# AI Travel Planner — Claude Code Implementation Specification

> **Specification v1.4 = this document (v1.3) + `docs/spec/AMENDMENT_A1_AWS_RAG.md` (2 November 2026; IMD-99 to IMD-116).** Read the amendment together with this file. Where they differ, the amendment wins. It moves hosting to AWS (Amazon ECS Express Mode, Amazon RDS PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector, Supabase for sign-in only) and adds the RAG pipeline (Gemini embeddings, pgvector retrieval, cited sources on itinerary items).

Version 1.3 (extensions, team plan v2 and execution protocol), 27 October 2026. Markdown edition of the specification PDF, for Claude Code and the planner; the content is the same, and diagrams are in the PDF. Sections are cited as §N; Appendix A holds the reference SQL (also in `docs/spec/sql/`).

# 1. Project execution overview

This specification turns the AI Travel Planner Design & Implementation Blueprint (version 1.0, 355 pages, "the blueprint") into the instructions from which Claude Code builds the application, one task and one sprint at a time. It is the single source of truth for scope, architecture, data and API contracts, tasks, tests and gates. The blueprint remains the background reference: when this specification cites "blueprint §N", that section explains why; this document says what to build. Where the two differ, this document wins and the difference is recorded in the decision register (Appendix B).

Ownership follows the team's Contribution Plan (version 2, 27 October 2026): each of the ten members owns 42 or 43 of the 427 points, every task card names its lead and its parts, and §14.3 to §14.5 and Appendix C give the allocation and the rules for shared cards. How to use it: read §1 to §4 once; read §5 to §9 when a task touches that layer; execute §10 part by part under the rules of §11 and §12, driven by the planner and Claude Code as Appendix D describes (every commit authored as the part's owner); verify with §13; pass the gates of §14; keep §15 current.

## 1.1 Product objective

A web application in which a signed-in traveller describes a trip (destination, dates, travellers, budget, pace, interests, must-visit places) and receives a day-wise itinerary that is feasible, costed and editable. Gemini proposes the plan from a shortlist of curated places; the backend checks every place, time, travel gap and price in code, recalculates all numbers, labels every estimate, and saves the plan with its warnings. The product stays usable when Gemini is unavailable through a rule-based fallback planner and saved sample itineraries (PD-12).

## 1.4 Approved technology stack

| Layer | Choice | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web | Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, dnd-kit, TanStack Query, react-hook-form + zod | Confirmed (baseline); TanStack Query, react-hook-form and zod Provisional |
| Map | MapLibre GL JS with OpenFreeMap tiles; list view fallback | Confirmed |
| API | Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, pydantic-settings | Confirmed; Python 3.12 Provisional |
| Data access | SQLAlchemy 2 (async) with psycopg 3, Alembic running versioned SQL files | Confirmed; driver and SQL-file approach Provisional (IMD-01) |
| Database and auth | Supabase Postgres and Supabase Auth; Supabase CLI local stack for development (IMD-03) | Confirmed; local stack Provisional |
| AI provider | Gemini API through `google-genai`, only behind `ModelProvider`; MOCK adapter; FINETUNED_MODEL stub | Confirmed (PD-01, PD-02) |
| Travel times | OpenRouteService with route cache and distance-based fallback | Confirmed (baseline) |
| Hosting and delivery | Vercel (web), Render (API Docker container), GitHub Actions | Confirmed (baseline) |
| Quality | pytest, Vitest + Testing Library, Playwright + axe, ruff, mypy, import-linter, ESLint, Prettier, pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks | Confirmed; gitleaks Provisional |

The stack is the blueprint's (blueprint §14.1) with no replacement. Four gaps the blueprint left open are filled with Provisional defaults: the async database driver, the typed API client generator (openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch, IMD-06), the command runner (Makefile, IMD-08) and the local authentication stack (IMD-03). The checks behind each are in Appendix B.

The API is a modular monolith of ten MVP backend modules (MOD-B01 to MOD-B10) plus the offline evaluation harness (MOD-B15); the web app has seven MVP modules (MOD-F01 to MOD-F07). Contracts between them are in §3; the repository layout is in §4.

## 1.6 Main end-to-end user journey

| Step | What the traveller does | What the system does | Screens and endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Signs up or signs in | Supabase Auth issues a session; the API verifies the token on every call | `/sign-up`, `/sign-in`; API-03 |
| 2 | Creates a trip and sets preferences and must-visit places | Validates and saves a draft trip and preferences | `/trips/new`; API-06, API-07, API-14 |
| 3 | Presses Generate (after the first-use privacy notice) | Creates a generation job (202), retrieves and ranks curated places, calls Gemini with a shortlist, validates and recalculates in code, repairs at most once, falls back to the rule-based planner if needed, saves plan, warnings, version and record in one transaction | `/trips/[tripId]/generate`; API-22, API-23 |
| 4 | Reads the itinerary, warnings and costs | Shows times, travel gaps, labelled prices, findings with suggested fixes and totals computed by the budget engine | `/itinerary`, `/costs`; API-24, API-33 |
| 5 | Moves, removes, adds, retimes, replaces or locks activities; regenerates a day | Each edit is one transaction that recalculates and revalidates; stale edits are refused | `/itinerary`; API-25 to API-32 |
| 6 | Saves a version, leaves, later reopens the trip | The latest itinerary and its warnings reappear exactly as saved | `/dashboard`, `/versions`; API-08, API-09, API-36 to API-38 |
| 7 | Views the final summary | Day-wise summary with labelled estimates; print view | `/summary`; API-35 |

## 1.8 Key technical decisions

| Decision | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini first, behind one interface | All model calls go through `ModelProvider`; vendor imports only in `app/ai/providers/gemini.py`; MOCK is the default outside staging and production | PD-01, PD-02 |
| The model only proposes | The model returns place IDs from the supplied shortlist, order, times and short notes; the backend validates IDs and recalculates times, travel gaps, prices and totals | PD-04, PD-14 |
| Always a usable path | Timeout, rate limit, outage, open breaker, unreadable output or an unusable plan after repair end in the rule-based plan, labelled as such; quota exhaustion and configuration errors end in `failed` with a one-click rule-based generation; an internal fault ends in `failed` and leaves the trip unchanged (blueprint §19.2.2) | PD-12 |
| Every generation is recorded | Provider, model ID, prompt version, schema versions, latency, usage and outcome in `ai_generations` | PD-05 |
| Fine-tuning is conditional | Stage 2 starts only after an evaluation gate and a recorded decision; nothing in Stage 1 depends on it | PD-03, PD-13 |
| One schema source, one API contract | SQL migration files define the schema; the generated OpenAPI document defines the API; drift tests fail the build | IMD-01, IMD-06 |
| Runs locally without accounts | Supabase CLI stack, MOCK provider, SAMPLE fixture destination and the routing fallback need no keys | IMD-03, IMD-09 |

## 1.10 Definition of a successful final demo and what must work by the end of week 8

The demo succeeds when, on the production deployment and with the release candidate tagged, a presenter completes the primary journey (§1.6, steps 1 to 7) with Gemini as the provider, then repeats step 3 with the provider failing and shows a labelled rule-based plan, and every number on screen comes from the backend with its label. A recorded backup video and the saved sample itineraries cover a hosting or provider outage (CHK-17).

By the end of week 8 the following must be working and evidenced in `docs/progress/` (each item is a pass/fail check of SG-8):

1. Sign-up, sign-in, sign-out; every protected route refuses a missing or foreign token; the two-user authorization suite passes (E2E-01, E2E-08).
2. Trip creation with validation, drafts, preferences and must-visit places; dashboard; reopening the latest itinerary (E2E-02, E2E-06).
3. Generation with Gemini on production through the job protocol, with records in `ai_generations`; MOCK in local and CI (E2E-03).
4. Validation with the 13 finding codes, bounded repair, the labelled rule-based fallback on provider failure or invalid output, and the paused-AI message with a rule-based option on quota exhaustion (E2E-04, E2E-07).
5. Editing: reorder (drag and keyboard), remove, add, retime, and the cut-list features that were kept; every edit recalculated in one transaction; stale edits refused (E2E-05).
6. Deterministic costs with breakdown and labels; travel times from OpenRouteService or the labelled fallback.
7. Final summary; accessible, responsive pages with recorded axe and keyboard results.
8. Every extension that was kept is demonstrable with its tests green; extensions that were cut are switched off and listed in the known limitations.
9. `make check` and `make e2e` green on the tagged commit; deployment smoke tests green on production (E2E-09); known limitations and deferred items documented.

# 2. Canonical feature and requirement register

This register is the only list of what the eight-week release implements. It reuses the blueprint IDs unchanged: catalogue items (F-, C-), functional requirements (FR-), quality requirements (NFR-), domain rules (DR-), stories (US-) and tests (TC-). The tables are generated from the blueprint registries and the task cards of §10, so the planned sprint, the implementing tasks and the tests always agree with §10 and §15.

**How Claude Code must read it.** A requirement is mandatory for the release only if its release code is MVP or MVP-S. Requirements with release code EXT (§2.5) are the extensions selected on 27 October 2026: each is built only by its own extension card in Sprints 5 to 7, behind its switch, and is switched off before any MVP cut-list item (IMD-47). MVP-S requirements are implemented exactly as their "shall" statement and acceptance criteria say, which is already the simplified behaviour; Claude Code must not extend them toward the full catalogue description. Requirements with codes T1, R2, PP or Stage 2 (§2.6) are never implemented as a side effect of another task. A cut-list item (§1.2) is implemented, but behind its switch.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Requirement and behaviour | Short title and the "shall" statement: the behaviour to implement |
| Priority | MoSCoW priority from the blueprint |
| Release | MVP or MVP-S (simplified MVP); EXT for the extensions in §2.5 |
| Owning module | Modules named by the implementing tasks (§3) |
| Depends on | Requirements delivered by the prerequisite tasks of the first implementing task |
| Acceptance criteria | The blueprint criteria, numbered AC1, AC2, ...; tasks and tests cite them by number |
| Sprint | Sprint of the first implementing task; later tasks may extend it (see Tasks) |
| Verification | Test cases (TC) with their type; the commands are in the task cards and §13 |

**AUTH — Accounts and access control**

| FR-001 | **Register an account.** The system shall let a visitor register with an email address and a password through Supabase Auth. | Must | MVP-S | MOD-F01 | FR-114, FR-124 | AC1: Given a valid unused email and a password of at least 8 characters, when the visitor submits the form, then an account exists and the visitor is signed in or asked to confirm the email, as configured.<br>AC2: Given an email that already has an account, when the visitor registers, then the form shows a non-revealing message and no second account is created.<br>AC3: Given an empty or weak password, when the form is submitted, then it is rejected with a field-level message. | Sprint 1 | IMP-109 | TC-051, TC-052, TC-053, TC-366 (+1) — Frontend 2, API 1, Review 1 |
| FR-002 | **Sign in, keep a session and sign out.** The system shall authenticate returning travellers, keep their session, and end it on sign-out. | Must | MVP-S | MOD-F01 | FR-114, FR-124 | AC1: Given valid credentials, when the traveller signs in, then the dashboard opens.<br>AC2: Given an expired or altered token, when any protected API call is made, then the API returns 401 and the app returns to sign-in.<br>AC3: Given the traveller has signed out, when they press Back, then no private trip data is shown. | Sprint 1 | IMP-109 | TC-054, TC-055, TC-056, TC-347 — Frontend 2, API 1, Security 1 |

## 2.3 Quality requirements

The 48 NFRs apply to the whole system; the tasks listed implement or measure them and the tests verify them. Targets are the blueprint's and remain Proposed until measured; no measurement exists yet.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NFR-001 | Performance | Page load on mobile | Largest Contentful Paint at most 2.5 s at the 75th percentile (proposed) | MVP | IMP-711 | TC-328 |
| NFR-002 | Performance | Non-AI API latency | p95 at most 500 ms excluding cold start (proposed) | MVP | IMP-304, IMP-309, IMP-410 (+2) | TC-329 |
| NFR-003 | Performance | Edit recalculation time | p95 at most 1.5 s (proposed) | MVP | IMP-407, IMP-408, IMP-409 (+6) | TC-330 |

## 2.4 Domain rules

The domain rules are enforced in code by the validation, budget, routing and trips modules (§9); each is tested through the requirements it supports.

| ID | Area | Rule | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DR-01 | Dates and time | Trip dates are calendar dates in the destination's time zone, and a trip covers the start date through the end date inclusive, so the number of days is end minus start plus one. | FR-007, FR-008 |
| DR-02 | Dates and time | Itinerary times are local times at the destination. Each destination stores an IANA time-zone name; times are stored without offsets and combined with the zone only for display and comparison. | FR-033 |
| DR-03 | Dates and time | A plan day runs between a day start and a day end (defaults proposed: 09:00 and 21:00). No activity starts before the day start or ends after the day end unless the traveller changes the limits. | FR-029, FR-053 |
| DR-04 | Dates and time | Durations are whole minutes. An activity lasts at least 15 and at most 480 minutes (proposed limits). | FR-063 |
| DR-05 | Dates and time | The MVP plans the first and last day like any other day and does not model arrival or departure travel time. The traveller can lock or remove items to allow for travel. Modelling travel days is an open decision (OD-09). | FR-034 |
| DR-06 | Opening hours | Opening hours are stored per weekday as one or more local-time intervals, and closed days are recorded explicitly. | FR-018, FR-052 |
| DR-07 | Opening hours | An interval that passes midnight is stored as ending on the next day and is checked against both days. | FR-052 |
| DR-08 | Opening hours | Hours carry a source, a verification status and a last-checked date. Seasonal and holiday changes are not modelled; hours older than a configured age (threshold to be set by the team) are shown as unverified. | FR-018 |
| DR-09 | Opening hours | Unknown hours are never treated as open or closed. The validator reports HOURS_UNVERIFIED and the interface shows "Hours unavailable". | FR-052 |
| DR-10 | Opening hours | A visit must fit inside one opening interval, from arrival to the end of the stay. A place flagged as always accessible has no hours check. | FR-052 |
| DR-11 | Routes | Travel time between consecutive activities uses the trip's travel mode (walking, local transport or car), and the mode is recorded with each estimate. | FR-078 |
| DR-12 | Routes | Every travel time has a source: routing_api or fallback_estimate. The fallback multiplies straight-line distance by a detour factor and divides by a mode speed; the factor and speeds are set by the team after comparing about 20 known routes in the demo cities. | FR-078, FR-079 |
| DR-13 | Routes | A buffer is added to every transfer beyond the travel time to cover queues, rest and delays (value configurable, larger for fallback estimates). | FR-051, FR-079 |
| DR-14 | Routes | A transfer is too short when the gap between activities is less than the travel time plus the buffer, and the validator reports TRANSFER_TOO_SHORT. | FR-051 |
| DR-15 | Routes | Travel times are estimates, not guarantees. The interface says "estimate" wherever they appear. | FR-117 |
| DR-16 | Budget | Money is stored in minor units or fixed-point decimals with an ISO 4217 currency code. The MVP uses one currency per trip and no live exchange rates. | FR-071 |
| DR-17 | Budget | The budget is the group total for the trip. This is the MVP rule: entering a budget per person is excluded from the MVP, and the form says that the amount is the group total. Cost per traveller is the total divided by the traveller count and is shown separately. | FR-071 |
| DR-18 | Budget | Costs fall into five categories: accommodation, food, transport, activities and other. | FR-073 |
| DR-19 | Budget | An activity cost is the place's price estimate scaled by the number of travellers. Separate child pricing is not modelled in the MVP. | FR-071 |
| DR-20 | Budget | Each line is rounded to the minor unit with round-half-up, and totals are sums of rounded lines, so displayed lines add up to displayed totals. | FR-071 |
| DR-21 | Budget | A contingency is a percentage of the estimate before contingency and has its own line. | FR-075 |
| DR-22 | Budget | The near-budget threshold is 90 percent of the budget (proposed, configurable). The plan is over budget when the estimate including contingency exceeds the budget. | FR-054, FR-074 |
| DR-23 | Accommodation | The MVP has no accommodation price source. The stay cost is the traveller's nightly stay budget multiplied by the number of nights (end date minus start date). | FR-072 |
| DR-24 | Accommodation | Accommodation recommendations (Release 2) are seeded, labelled estimates with outbound links, and never claim availability or room prices. | FR-084, FR-085 |
| DR-25 | Accommodation | Check-in and check-out times are not scheduled by the MVP. | FR-072 |
| DR-26 | Accessibility | The MVP accessibility preference means step-free access required. A place is marked yes, no or unknown; with the preference on, unknown places are excluded, except a must-visit place, which stays with a warning. | FR-009, FR-027 |
| DR-27 | Accessibility | Accessibility information is a labelled fact with source and date. The product does not certify accessibility. | FR-019 |
| DR-28 | Accessibility | The interface targets WCAG 2.2 level AA success criteria, without claiming a full audit unless one is done. | FR-025 |
| DR-29 | Expenses | Recorded expenses may be incomplete, and every expense view says so. | FR-104 |
| DR-30 | Expenses | An expense counts toward the remaining budget only after the traveller confirms it. Extracted receipt values stay unconfirmed until reviewed. | FR-101 |
| DR-31 | Expenses | An expense in another currency uses a conversion rate entered by the traveller and labelled as entered by them. No live rates are used. | FR-103 |
| DR-32 | Bookings | A booking task reminds the traveller to arrange something outside the product. The product takes no bookings and no payments. | FR-107 |
| DR-33 | Bookings | A confirmation reference typed by the traveller is shown as "recorded by you" and never as verified. | FR-110 |
| DR-34 | Bookings | A task is essential when the trip is impaired without it, recommended when it reduces risk or cost, and optional otherwise. | FR-107 |
| DR-35 | Data reliability | Every fact has a source, a verification status and, where one exists, a last-checked date. In the MVP the data is sample or estimated, and nothing is labelled live or verified. | FR-076, FR-117 |
| DR-36 | Data reliability | The language model is not an authoritative source for any fact named in PR-01. Displayed facts come from the places table or the traveller; model text sits in AI-written fields. | FR-035 |

# 3. Architecture and module contracts

This section is the single source of truth for components, boundaries and module interfaces. Field-level schemas are in §5 (database), §6 (API) and §8 (AI). Background and alternatives are in blueprint §13 and §15; they are not repeated here.

## 3.1 System context

The browser talks to two systems only: Supabase Auth (sign-up, sign-in, session refresh) and the FastAPI backend. The backend is the only component that reaches the database, the AI provider and the routing service. The model never sees credentials, user identifiers or database access.

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: System context. Only the backend reaches the database, Gemini, OpenRouteService and the extension data services (dashed). (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 3. System context. Only the backend reaches the database, Gemini, OpenRouteService and the extension data services (dashed).
:::

| External system | Called by | Mandatory for the MVP | When unavailable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supabase Auth | Browser (sessions); backend (key set only, if JWKS mode) | Yes | Sign-in impossible; public pages still load |
| Supabase Postgres | Backend only | Yes | API-02 reports not ready (503); API returns 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| Gemini API | `app/ai/providers/gemini.py` only | No (fallback exists) | Rule-based plan with outcome `fallback_rule_based` (§8) |
| OpenRouteService | `app/routing/client.py` only | No | Distance-based estimate labelled Estimate (§9) |
| OpenFreeMap tiles | Browser only | No | List view instead of the map |
| Open-Meteo forecast (EXT) | `app/weather/client.py` only | No (extension `rain_swap`) | "Forecast unavailable"; no rain flags or swap suggestion; plan unchanged (§9.3.9) |
| MediaWiki API: Wikivoyage, Wikipedia (EXT) | `app/context/client.py` only, from the refresh job | No (extension `context_cards`) | Cached card kept until it expires, else no card (§9) |

## 3.2 Components

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: Backend and web components. Arrows show allowed call direction. (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 4. Backend and web components. Arrows show allowed call direction.
:::

| Layer | Contents | May import | Must not |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routers (`router.py`) | FastAPI routes, request/response models, `CurrentUser` dependency, flag check | Services, `schemas`, `core` | Run SQL, call vendors, hold business rules |
| Services (`service.py`, `jobs.py`, `pipeline.py`) | Use cases, transaction boundaries, orchestration | Domain, own repository, lower-ranked services (§3.9), `ai.factory`, `routing.service` | Return ORM objects to routers |
| Domain (`domain.py`, `rules.py`, `engine.py`, `ranking.py`, `grouping.py`, `fallback_planner.py`, `estimate.py`, `repair.py`; extensions: `optimise.py`, `swap.py`, `today.py`, `fit.py`, `packing_rules.py`) | Pure functions over Pydantic/data classes | `schemas`, other domain files | Import FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, httpx, vendor SDKs; perform I/O |
| Repositories (`repository.py`, `db/models/`) | SQLAlchemy queries; owned resources always filtered by `user_id` | `db` | Business rules |
| Clients and adapters | `ai/providers/*`, `routing/client.py`, `weather/client.py`, `context/client.py` (extensions) | `schemas`, `core.config` | Be imported except by `ai/factory.py` (adapters) or the owning module's `service.py` (clients) |

## 3.3 Frontend and backend boundary

| Concern | Frontend (`apps/web`) | Backend (`apps/api`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | Holds the Supabase session; sends `Authorization: Bearer` | Verifies the token; user id only from the token |
| Validation | Mirrors server rules with zod for early feedback only | Authoritative: Pydantic models and domain rules; 422 envelope |
| Itinerary, times, prices, totals, routes | Displays server values and labels; never computes or invents them | Computes, validates and persists every value |
| Generation | Starts a job, polls status, renders outcome notice | Runs the job, calls the provider, validates, falls back, saves |
| Errors | Maps `error.code` to a message; shows `request_id` | Produces the error envelope (§6) |
| Secrets | Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values | All keys (Gemini, ORS, database, JWT secret) |
| Database | No direct table access | Sole writer; RLS is a second lock (§5) |

## 3.4 Authentication and authorization flow

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: Authenticated request. Ownership is enforced in the API and again by row-level security. (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 5. Authenticated request. Ownership is enforced in the API and again by row-level security.
:::

Rules (binding):

1. Every route in `app/*/router.py` declares exactly one access class: public (API-01, API-02), signed-in reference data (API-06, API-16, API-17) or owned resource (all other MVP routes). `tests/authz/test_ownership.py` enumerates the OpenAPI routes and fails if a route is missing from its access table.
2. `CurrentUser` (in `app/auth/deps.py`) returns the user id from the verified token: header missing, malformed, expired, wrong audience or bad signature → 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`.
3. Owned resources are loaded by repository functions that take `user_id` as a required argument; child resources (item, version, generation) are resolved to their trip first. Not found and not owned are the same answer: 404 `NOT_FOUND`.
4. A `profiles` row is created on the first authenticated call (`get_or_create_profile` in `CurrentUser`), not by a database trigger; it must exist before any `trips` insert because `trips.user_id` references `profiles.id`.
5. The browser roles hold no table privileges (migration 0005); the backend connects with the database owner connection, so API filters are the primary protection.
6. The web app refreshes the session once on a 401 and then redirects to `/sign-in`.

## 3.5 AI generation flow (overview)

Generation is an asynchronous job (IMD-12). Detailed steps, schemas, prompts, retries and repair are in §8; the API lifecycle is in §6.

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: One generation request across components (detail in §8 and §6). (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 6. One generation request across components (detail in §8 and §6).
:::

What the model decides and what code decides: the model proposes the order of known places per day and short AI-labelled notes; code supplies candidate places, opening hours, prices, travel times, totals and every validation result (§8).

## 3.6 Edit flow and database interaction

Manual edits are synchronous. Each edit request carries `plan_revision`; the itinerary service runs one transaction:

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: One edit (API-25 to API-29): one transaction, recalculated server-side. (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 7. One edit (API-25 to API-29): one transaction, recalculated server-side.
:::

| Transaction boundary | Opened by | Writes in one commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create or update a trip with preferences | `trips.service` | `trips`, `trip_preferences` |
| Start generation | `generation.service.start` | `ai_generations` insert (after the per-trip row lock and cap count) |
| Finish generation | `generation.pipeline` save step | `itinerary_days`, `itinerary_items`, `itinerary_warnings`, `itinerary_versions`, `trips.plan_revision`, `ai_generations` completion |
| Edit, add, remove, replace, lock | `itinerary.service` | Items of the affected day(s), warnings, `trips.plan_revision` |
| Save or restore a version | `itinerary.versions` | `itinerary_versions` (restore also rewrites days, items, warnings, revision) |
| Budget settings | `budget.service` | `budget_settings` |
| Route cache | `routing.service` | `route_cache` upsert, outside the edit transaction (a cache write never rolls back an edit) |

Rules: services receive an `AsyncSession` from `db.session`; only the outermost service call commits; repositories never commit. External calls (Gemini, ORS) are made outside open write transactions, except the final save step, which runs after all external calls have returned.

## 3.7 External-service boundaries

| Boundary | Single entry point | Timeout | Failure mapped to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini | `ai/providers/gemini.py` through `ai/factory.py` | `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_S` (35 s) per call, at most `GEMINI_MAX_RETRIES` (1) retry | `ProviderError` subclasses (§8); never an HTTP error to the browser |
| OpenRouteService | `routing/client.py` through `routing/service.py` | `ORS_TIMEOUT_S` (8 s, Provisional) | Distance estimate with `travel_source = fallback_estimate` |
| Supabase Auth key set | `auth/tokens.py` | 5 s fetch timeout; key set cached 10 minutes (IMD-04) | Key set unreachable and no cached key matches: 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` on protected routes; readiness unaffected |
| Postgres | `db/session.py` | Pool timeouts from settings | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| Open-Meteo forecast (EXT, IMP-710) | `weather/client.py` through `weather/service.py`; cached 3 hours in `weather_cache` | `WEATHER_TIMEOUT_S` (8 s) | No forecast: API-68 returns days without flags; the plan is never changed automatically |
| MediaWiki API, Wikivoyage and Wikipedia (EXT, IMP-713) | `context/client.py`, called only by the refresh job in `context/jobs.py`; serial requests with `WIKI_USER_AGENT` | Constant in `context/client.py`; job only, no user request waits on it | No card: API-72/73 return 404 and the drawer shows nothing extra |
| Flight and hotel booking providers | None | — | Not integrated: in-app booking is excluded (§1.3 and IMD-46) |

## 3.8 Failure and fallback paths

| Failure | Detected in | Behaviour | What the user sees | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini timeout, 429, 5xx | Gemini adapter | Bounded retry, then breaker (transient); pipeline uses the rule-based planner; `model_id` stays the configured model (IMD-43) | Plan labelled "built by rules" (FallbackNotice) | FR-037, FR-047 |
| Gemini quota exhausted (daily quota or empty balance) | Gemini adapter | No retry; breaker open 15 min; generation `failed`, `provider_quota_exhausted`, and the same for every AI generation while the breaker is open (no automatic fallback, IMD-44); old plan kept | "AI generation is paused for today" with a "Build without AI" button | FR-037, FR-046 |
| Gemini invalid JSON or unknown place ids | Output validation | Deterministic repair, at most one model retry, then fallback | Repaired plan with notice, or rule-based plan | FR-032, FR-057, FR-036 |
| Gemini key missing or invalid | Settings check / adapter | No retry; generation `failed` with `failure_reason = config_error` (blueprint §19.2.2); breaker open until restart, and later AI generations end the same way (IMD-44) | Paused-AI message with a "Build without AI" button (mode `rule_based`); readiness shows provider `down` | FR-124 |
| Daily cap reached | `generation.service.start` | No job created | 429 `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` with reset time | FR-046 |
| Job stuck (> 150 s) | Reaper in `generation/jobs.py` | Mark `failed`, reason `internal`; plan unchanged | Error with retry button | NFR-004 |
| ORS down or quota used | Routing client | Distance estimate | "Estimated travel time (distance based)" | FR-079 |
| Map tiles fail | `MapPanel` | Hide map | List view | NFR-010 |
| Stale edit | Itinerary service | Nothing written | Reload prompt | FR-069 |
| Database unreachable | Session / readiness | 503 | ErrorState with request id | NFR-008 |
| Fallback planner itself fails | Pipeline | Generation `failed`, reason `internal`; old plan kept | Error with retry button | FR-036 |
| Forecast unavailable or outside 16 days (EXT) | `weather/service.py` | No rain flags, no swap suggestion; plan unchanged | "Forecast unavailable" in ForecastBanner (outside the 16-day window: "No forecast yet for this date") | FR-131 |
| Wiki unreachable, page missing or licence text absent (EXT) | `context/jobs.py` | No card stored or the old card kept until `expires_at` | Drawer without a context card | FR-134 |
| Assistive AI call fails, is rejected by validation or the assist cap is reached (EXT: intake, explanation, packing refinement) | MOD-B05 and the calling service | Call logged in `ai_assist_calls` (`failed` or `rejected`); nothing saved; the core plan is unaffected; cap gives 429 `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` | The extension shows "unavailable"; the form, plan or rule-based packing list remains usable | FR-128, FR-129, FR-135 |
| Optimise finds no saving of 5 minutes or adds an error finding (EXT) | `itinerary/optimise.py` | Preview reports no change; nothing written | "This day is already in a good order" | FR-130 |

## 3.9 Module ownership and dependency direction

Service-level dependencies form a strict order; a module may call only modules of a lower rank (domain files of any module may be used by any service, because they are pure). This removes the itinerary↔generation, budget↔itinerary and validation↔itinerary cycles that a package-level reading of the blueprint would create.

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: Service dependency order (arrows point to the callee). No cycles. (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 8. Service dependency order (arrows point to the callee). No cycles.
:::

| Rank | Module (service level) | Writes tables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | MOD-B01 core, MOD-D01 db, `app/schemas` | none |
| 1 | MOD-B02 auth, MOD-B04 places, MOD-B05 ai, MOD-B10 routing | `profiles`; `destinations`, `data_sources`, `places`, `place_opening_hours` (seed/import only), `trip_places`; `ai_assist_calls` (EXT); `route_cache` |
| 2 | MOD-B03 trips (incl. API-64 intake, EXT), MOD-B16 forecast service (EXT), MOD-B17 context cards (EXT) | `trips` (except `plan_revision`), `trip_preferences`; `weather_cache`; `context_cards` |
| 3 | MOD-B08 itinerary (incl. API-65 to API-67, API-69, API-70, EXT) | `itinerary_days` (incl. `explanation*` columns), `itinerary_items`, `itinerary_warnings`, `itinerary_versions`, `trips.plan_revision` |
| 4 | MOD-B09 budget (API-33/34, API-71 EXT), MOD-B07 validation (API-32), MOD-B16 rain advice (API-68, EXT), MOD-B12 prep: packing (API-43, API-74, API-75, EXT) | `budget_settings`; none (warnings written through B08); none; `checklist_items` |
| 5 | MOD-B06 generation (API-22, 23, 30, 31; API-63 ranking explanation, EXT) | `ai_generations` |
| 6 | MOD-B15 evaluation | files under `eval/` only |

MOD-B16 has two levels: the forecast service (client, cache) sits at rank 2 because it reads destination coordinates through MOD-B04, and the rain-advice use case behind API-68 sits at rank 4 because it reads the plan through MOD-B08. MOD-B17 sits at rank 2 for the same reason as the forecast service. Assistive AI calls go only through `ai/factory.py` like generation calls. Placement decisions (IMD-13): the handlers of API-30 and API-31 (regenerate a day / the whole plan) live in `generation/router.py`, because they start generation jobs; their paths are unchanged. API-32 (re-validate) lives in `validation/router.py` and calls `itinerary.service.revalidate`. Pure logic of validation (`validation/rules.py`, `validator.py`, `repair.py`), budget (`budget/engine.py`), routing estimate (`routing/estimate.py`) and generation (`ranking.py`, `grouping.py`, `fallback_planner.py`) is domain code usable by any service.

# 4. Repository structure and conventions

One repository, two applications (`apps/web`, `apps/api`), one database schema and one command runner. There are no separate services per feature. Before creating a file, Claude Code checks whether it already exists and extends it; the paths below are binding.

## 4.2 Naming conventions

| Item | Convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python modules, functions, variables | `snake_case`; classes `PascalCase`; constants `UPPER_SNAKE` | `build_request`, `GenerationRequest`, `MAX_ITEMS` |
| TypeScript | `camelCase` values, `PascalCase` components and types; one component per file named like the component | `DayColumn.tsx`, `useTrip()` |
| API JSON fields and query parameters | `snake_case`, identical to the Pydantic field names | `plan_revision`, `start_date` |
| Enumerated values | Lower `snake_case` strings, except provider names (`GEMINI`, `MOCK`, `FINETUNED_MODEL`) and finding/error codes (`UPPER_SNAKE`) | `fallback_rule_based`, `STALE_PLAN` |
| Database | Tables plural `snake_case`; columns `snake_case`; PK `id` (UUID) except 1:1 tables keyed by `trip_id`; FK `<entity>_id`; indexes `ix_<table>_<cols>`; checks named where the SQL names them | `itinerary_items.day_id` |
| URL paths | `/api/v1/` + plural nouns, kebab-case for multi-word segments, path ids named `{trip_id}` etc. | `/api/v1/trips/{trip_id}/saved-places/{place_id}` |
| Web routes | Lower case, kebab-case, dynamic segments `[tripId]` | `/trips/[tripId]/itinerary` |
| Environment variables | `UPPER_SNAKE`; browser-visible only with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` | `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_S` |
| Branches | `feat\|fix\|chore/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>`, one branch per task part (§14.4) | `feat/IMP-409-move-api`, `feat/IMP-409-move-controls` |
| Commits | Conventional Commits starting with the task ID; author and committer are the part's owner (name and email from the team table); exactly one author, no `Co-authored-by:` line, no mention of AI tools (IMD-61) | `feat(itinerary): IMP-409 keyboard move controls` |
| Pull requests | One task part per PR; the title names the part; assigned to the part owner with the named reviewer; the template lists linked IDs, what changed, tests run with results, screenshots, contract and migration questions; merged with Rebase and merge only (IMD-63) | `IMP-409 · move-controls part` |
| Migrations | Files `000N_<concern>.sql`, `down/000N_<concern>.down.sql` and `versions/000N_<concern>.py`; Alembic revision id `000N`; downgrade runs the down SQL file; one migration per PR; never edit a merged migration | `0004_ai_and_plan`, revision `0004` |

## 4.3 Code organization

**Backend module layout.** Each backend package under `apps/api/app/` uses the same file roles; a module creates only the files it needs.

| File | Role | Layer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `router.py` | FastAPI `APIRouter`; request/response models from `schemas.py`; dependencies `CurrentUser`, `require_feature` | Router |
| `schemas.py` | Pydantic v2 request and response models (`extra="forbid"` on requests) | Router/contract |
| `service.py` | Use cases; opens transactions; calls domain, own repository and lower-ranked services (§3.9) | Service |
| `repository.py` | SQLAlchemy queries; owned queries require `user_id` | Repository |
| `domain.py` (or named domain files) | Pure rules, no I/O | Domain |
| `client.py` / `providers/*.py` | External HTTP or SDK calls | Adapter |

**Backend tests.** `tests/unit/<module>/test_<topic>.py` (pure, no database, mock provider); `tests/contract/` (provider contract, recorded Gemini responses, OpenAPI contract); `tests/api/test_<area>.py` (HTTP + migrated PostgreSQL); `tests/authz/` (two-user ownership); `tests/smoke/test_deployed.py` (against a URL). Shared fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` (`auth.py` token minting, `db.py` migrated database with the auth stub when schema `auth` is absent, `factories.py`, `provider_recordings/`).

**Web layout.** Pages in `app/` only compose area components and call hooks from `lib/api/queries.ts`; they hold no fetch logic. Area folders under `components/` (`shell`, `trips`, `places`, `generation`, `itinerary`, `map`, `costs`, `versions`, `profile`, `states`, `labels`, `ui`). An area may import `ui`, `states`, `labels` and `lib/*`; cross-area imports are limited to `itinerary → places, map, costs, generation`. Enforced with ESLint `no-restricted-imports` patterns (Provisional). Component tests mirror the folder: `tests/unit/<area>/<ComponentName>.test.tsx`.

## 4.4 Import boundaries (`apps/api/.importlinter`, run by `make imports`)

| Contract | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Layers | For every module: `router` may import `service` and `schemas`; `service` may import domain, `repository`, `schemas`; domain and `repository` never import `service` or `router` |
| Pure domain | EXT `itinerary.optimise`, `itinerary.swap`, `itinerary.today`, `budget.fit`, `prep.packing_rules` as well as `validation.rules`, `validation.validator`, `validation.repair`, `budget.engine`, `routing.estimate`, `generation.ranking`, `generation.grouping`, `generation.fallback_planner`, `trips.domain` must not import `fastapi`, `sqlalchemy`, `httpx`, `google.genai` or any `repository`/`service` |
| Vendor isolation | `google.genai` is imported only by `app.ai.providers.gemini`; concrete adapters are imported only by `app.ai.factory` (NFR-031) |
| Routing isolation | `httpx` calls to OpenRouteService only in `app.routing.client`; EXT: Open-Meteo only in `app.weather.client`, MediaWiki only in `app.context.client` |
| Service order | Services import only services of a lower rank (§3.9): e.g. `app.itinerary` must not import `app.generation`, `app.budget.service` or `app.validation.router` |
| Booking | No `app.booking` package and no booking, payment or partner SDK dependency (in-app booking is excluded, §1.3 and IMD-46) |
| Not-MVP packages | Any import of `app.sharing`, `app.expenses`, `app.assistant` fails; `app.prep` may be imported only by its own router (EXT packing) |

## 4.5 Environment separation and variables

| Aspect | Local (developer) | Test / CI | Staging | Production |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_ENV` | `local` | `test` | `staging` | `production` |
| Database | Supabase CLI local Postgres (`127.0.0.1:54322`) or compose `db` | Compose/service `db` (postgres:16) + auth stub; blank, migrated per run | Hosted Supabase staging project | Hosted Supabase production project (OD-15: one or two projects) |
| Auth | Supabase CLI local Auth, HS256 secret from `supabase status -o env` | Minted HS256 test tokens; e2e uses the local stack | Hosted Supabase Auth (JWKS or secret, OD-06) | Same as staging |
| AI provider | `MOCK` with `MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO` (personal key optional for `make live-smoke`) | `MOCK` only; no key exists in PR CI | `GEMINI`, spending-controlled key, synthetic inputs; may run `MOCK` with a scenario for the failure demo (IMD-27, IMD-33) | `GEMINI`, billed key with spending control; `MOCK` refused at start-up |
| Routing | Optional key; estimate otherwise | No key; estimate and respx mocks | Staging key | Production key |
| Data | `data/fixtures/sampleton` + optional curated sets | Fixture only | Curated destinations | Curated destinations |
| URLs | Web `http://localhost:3000`, API `http://localhost:8000` | In-runner | Vercel staging URL, Render staging URL | Vercel production URL, Render production URL |
| Secrets live in | Untracked `apps/api/.env`, `apps/web/.env.local` | GitHub Actions (none for PR jobs) | Render / Vercel environment settings | Render / Vercel environment settings |
| Deployed by | The member | The pipeline | `deploy-staging.yml` on merge to `main` | Kirtan by hand from a tag via `deploy-production.yml` |

Variable names are fixed in `.env.example` below; each environment differs only in values. The backend reads settings once through `core/config.py` and applies the start-up checks of FR-124 (§8).

| Variable | Used by | Local / test value | Staging and production rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_ENV`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN` | API settings | `local` or `test`, `INFO`, `http://localhost:3000`, `60` | Exact web origin only (NFR-015) |
| `BUILD_VERSION`, `PORT` | Health version; container port | `dev`; `8000` | Set by CI (commit SHA); `PORT` is set by Render |
| `FEATURES_DISABLED`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURES_DISABLED` | Cut-list switches (IMD-11); EXT names `ranking_explain`, `nl_intake`, `day_explain`, `optimise_order`, `rain_swap`, `today_view`, `budget_fit`, `context_cards`, `packing` | empty | Same list in API and web |
| `DATABASE_URL`, `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | API, tests, `make db-migrate` | Local stack or compose `db` | Secret; staging and production Supabase connection strings |
| `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_JWKS_URL`, `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` | Token verification (IMD-04) | Local stack URL and JWT secret | Secret; JWKS or secret per OD-06 |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` | Web app (public by design) | Local stack, `http://localhost:8000/api/v1` | Only these and the switch list may reach the browser |
| `ORS_API_KEY`, `ORS_TIMEOUT_S` | Routing client | Empty (distance estimate), `8` | Secret key |
| `AI_PROVIDER`, `PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION`, `MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO` | Provider factory, prompt registry, mock (IMD-27) | `MOCK`, `v1`, `ok` | `GEMINI` in production (MOCK refused); scenarios ignored in production |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_MODEL_ID`, `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_S`, `GEMINI_MAX_RETRIES` | Gemini adapter | Empty, empty, `35`, `1` | Secret key; start-up refuses empty or `<` values and timeout × (retries + 1) > 70 |
| `AI_TEMPERATURE`, `AI_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS`, `AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, `AI_DAILY_GENERATIONS_PER_USER`, `AI_DAILY_GENERATIONS_GLOBAL` | Limits and caps | `0.4`, empty, empty, `10`, `200` | Caps and token limits required (NFR-037) |
| `AI_DAILY_ASSIST_CALLS_PER_USER` | Assist-call cap (EXT: intake, day explanation, packing refinement) | `30` (Proposed) | Required; 429 `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` when reached |

| `WIKI_USER_AGENT` | MediaWiki client (EXT) | Placeholder | Required in staging and production when `context_cards` is enabled; descriptive with a team contact |
| `FINETUNED_ENDPOINT_URL`, `FINETUNED_API_KEY`, `FINETUNED_MODEL_NAME` | Stage 2 placeholders | Empty | Empty in Stage 1 |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | E2E user fixture only | From `supabase status -o env` | Never set outside the local stack |
| `SEED_DIRS` | Makefile variable for `make seed` (extra curated directories) | Empty (fixture only) | Curated directories when seeding staging |

Planning constants (day window, meal windows, pace presets, budget-near threshold, preference mapping version) are code, not environment variables (IMD-29). Deployment migrations run from the deploy workflow, never on container start (IMD-38).

| Contract | Defined in (source of truth) | Generated or checked artefact | Check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Database schema | `apps/api/migrations/sql/000N_*.sql` (IMD-01) | ORM models in `app/db/models/` | `tests/api/test_schema_drift.py` |
| HTTP API | Pydantic models in `app/*/schemas.py` and `app/schemas/common.py` | `contracts/openapi.v1.json` → `apps/web/lib/api/schema.d.ts` (openapi-typescript) | `make openapi-check` in CI |
| AI request/response | `app/schemas/ai.py` (gr-1, io-1, findings; EXT ti-1, de-1, ps-1) | `contracts/ai/gr-1.schema.json`, `io-1.schema.json`; EXT `ti-1`, `de-1`, `ps-1` `.schema.json` (structured-output schemas sent to Gemini) | `make openapi-check`; contract tests |
| Prompt templates | `app/ai/prompts/templates/<task>/<version>/` | Version recorded in `ai_generations` | `tests/unit/ai/test_registry.py` |
| Client-side form rules | `apps/web/lib/validation/*.ts` (zod), mirroring the server limits | None (server remains authoritative) | Component tests + API 422 tests |
| Labels and enumerations | `app/schemas/labels.py` | Appear in OpenAPI enums → web types | `make openapi-check` |

Commands are defined once in the `Makefile` (§4.7); CLAUDE.md (§12) and the task cards (§10) use only those target names.

## 4.7 Makefile targets

The `Makefile` (IMD-08) is the only command vocabulary; CLAUDE.md (§12.1), the task cards (§10) and the tests (§13) use these names. `ARGS` passes extra arguments to the wrapped tool, for example `make test-api ARGS='-k trips'`, `make e2e ARGS='--grep @smoke'` or `make seed ARGS='--check --strict'`. Targets that are not yet created are added by the task that first needs them (IMP-101 creates the file with all targets that have a tool behind them).

| Target | Runs (underlying command) | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| make setup | create apps/api/.venv, `pip install -e "apps/api[dev]"`; `npm ci --prefix apps/web`; `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` (optional flag) | Python 3.12, Node LTS |
| make stack-up / make stack-down | `supabase start` / `supabase stop` | Docker, Supabase CLI |
| make db-up / make db-down | `docker compose up -d db` / `docker compose down` | Docker |
| make db-migrate | `cd apps/api && alembic upgrade head` (DATABASE_URL) | db |
| make db-reset | refuses unless APP_ENV is local or test; drops and recreates schema public (and data), then db-migrate and seed | db |
| make seed | `python -m app.places.seed data/fixtures/sampleton` (+ any `data/places/*` given as SEED_DIRS) | migrated db |
| make api | `uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000` | env |
| make web | `npm run dev --prefix apps/web` (port 3000) | env |
| make lint | `ruff check apps/api && ruff format --check apps/api && npm run lint --prefix apps/web && npm run format:check --prefix apps/web` | |
| make typecheck | `mypy apps/api/app && npm run typecheck --prefix apps/web` | |
| make imports | `lint-imports` (config apps/api/.importlinter) | |
| make test-unit | `pytest apps/api/tests/unit` | none |
| make test-contract | `pytest apps/api/tests/contract -m "not live"` | none |
| make test-api | `pytest apps/api/tests/api` | db (TEST_DATABASE_URL) |
| make test-authz | `pytest apps/api/tests/authz` | db |
| make test-web | `npm run test --prefix apps/web` (vitest run) | |
| make test | test-unit + test-contract + test-api + test-authz + test-web | db |
| make e2e | `npx playwright test` in apps/web; starts the API with AI_PROVIDER=MOCK and the web app, unless `BASE_URL` is set, in which case it runs against that deployment (smoke) | stack-up, seeded |
| make openapi / make openapi-check | export OpenAPI + AI JSON Schemas, regenerate web types / fail if stale | |
| make eval | `python -m app.evaluation.run --dataset $(DATASET) --provider $(PROVIDER)`; defaults PROVIDER=MOCK, DATASET=trips/v1 | |
| make check | lint + typecheck + imports + openapi-check + test | db |
| make smoke | `pytest apps/api/tests/smoke --base-url $(URL)` | deployed URL |
| make live-smoke | `pytest apps/api/tests/contract -m live` (needs GEMINI_API_KEY; never in PR CI) | key |

pytest markers: `live` (needs a real provider key; skipped otherwise; run only by `make live-smoke`) and `slow`. The test database URL is `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (default `postgresql+psycopg://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/travel_test`).

# 5. Database implementation specification

The MVP uses one PostgreSQL database (Supabase in staging and production, the Supabase CLI stack or a plain PostgreSQL 16 container locally and in CI, IMD-03) with 15 tables. The extension release (EXT, Sprints 5 to 7) adds four tables (`checklist_items`, `ai_assist_calls`, `weather_cache`, `context_cards`) and three columns on `itinerary_days` in migrations 0007 to 0010, for 19 tables in total; each extension table is created only by its own task (§5.5). The SQL files of Appendix A are the only definition of the schema (IMD-01). This section states how the schema is used, owned, migrated, seeded, reset and checked. Background and alternatives are in blueprint §16; they are not repeated.

**What has been executed.** On 2026-10-25 the test stub and migrations 0001 to 0006 of Appendix A were loaded in order into an empty scratch PostgreSQL 16.15 server (with an `alembic_version` table present, as Alembic would create it). The result was 15 MVP tables plus `alembic_version`. Three inserts were accepted, and two deliberately invalid inserts were rejected by `ai_generations_check` and `ux_versions_name`. The nine `updated_at` triggers were present. `anon` and `authenticated` had no privilege on `trips` or `alembic_version`. All six downgrade files then ran in reverse order, and migrations 0001 to 0006 were applied again cleanly. After the final changes to migration 0004 (IMD-22, IMD-42) the cycle was repeated on a fresh scratch PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster the same day: 15 tables after the upgrade, 0 after the downgrades, 15 again after re-applying; a completed generation row with a `failure_reason` and two invalid warning rows (MUST_VISIT_MISSING without `place_id`, OVERLAP with `place_id`) were rejected, and the matching valid rows were accepted. On 2026-10-27 the extension migrations were checked the same way on another fresh scratch PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster: the stub and migrations 0001 to 0010 gave 19 tables plus `alembic_version` and ten `updated_at` triggers; all ten downgrade files ran in reverse order to 0 tables; 0001 to 0010 then applied again to 19 tables. Five deliberately invalid inserts were rejected (a `day_explanation` assist call without a trip, a context card with a non-wiki URL, a rule packing item with status `suggested`, a duplicate rule label, and an explanation without its revision), a trip-intake assist call without a trip and an AI-suggested packing item were accepted, and `anon` and `authenticated` had no privilege on the four new tables. The cluster was deleted afterwards. These were scratch servers only. Nothing has been run on Supabase, and the first Supabase run (IMP-112, IMP-106) may expose differences that must be fixed and recorded.
