The extension tables are marked EXT. `context_cards` is not drawn: its `subject_id` refers to a place or a destination according to `subject_type`, so it has no foreign key and the context service checks that the subject exists and is active before writing (IMP-713). The explanation columns of `itinerary_days` (0008) add no relationship.

## 5.2 Tables

There is one writer per table (blueprint §15.3). Any other module that needs a change calls the writer's service. "Owner" is the row owner used for authorization. The `auth.users` table belongs to Supabase Auth, and `profiles.id` equals `auth.users.id`.

| Table | Purpose | Writer | Key columns | Foreign keys (cardinality, on delete) | Row owner and RLS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `destinations` | Supported destinations | MOD-B04 seed only | `slug` unique, `timezone`, `currency`, bounding box, `is_active`, `is_sample` | none | Shared; read where `is_active` |
| `data_sources` | Provenance of every place | MOD-B04 seed only | `name` unique, `source_type`, `licence`, `url`, `retrieved_on` | none | Shared; read |
| `places` | Curated or sample places | MOD-B04 seed only | `category`, `tags[]`, `lat`/`lon`, `typical_duration_min`, `price_min`/`price_max`/`price_currency`, `price_label`, `hours_label`, `verification_status`, suitability flags | destination 1:N restrict; source 1:N restrict | Shared; read where `is_active` |
| `place_opening_hours` | Weekly hours (ISO weekday, local time) | MOD-B04 seed only | `weekday`, `is_closed`, `open_time`, `close_time`, `closes_next_day` | place 1:N cascade | Shared; read |
| `profiles` | Profile of an Auth user | MOD-B02 | `display_name`, `preferred_currency`, `ai_notice_ack_at`, `default_preferences` | `auth.users` 1:1 cascade | Own row (`id = auth.uid()`) |
| `trips` | Trip with status and plan revision | MOD-B03 (except `plan_revision`, which MOD-B08 writes directly inside its edit and save transactions) | `title`, `status` draft, ready or archived; dates; generated `num_days` 1 to 14; `adults`, `children`, `group_needs[]`; `budget_amount`/`budget_currency`; `plan_revision`; `plan_stale`; `deleted_at` | profile 1:N cascade; destination 1:N restrict | `user_id`; owner policy excludes soft-deleted rows |
| `trip_preferences` | One preferences row per trip | MOD-B03 | `interests[]`, `pace`, `budget_priority`, `transport_pref`, `accommodation_type`, `step_free_required`, `notes` | trip 1:1 cascade | Via `owns_trip(trip_id)` |
| `trip_places` | Must-visit, saved and rejected places | MOD-B04 (must-visit via the MOD-B03 preferences service) | `relation` must_visit, saved or rejected; unique (`trip_id`, `place_id`) | trip 1:N cascade; place 1:N restrict | Via `owns_trip` |
| `budget_settings` | Allowances and contingency | MOD-B09 | `transport_allowance_per_day`, `stay_budget_per_night`, `contingency_pct` (default 10) | trip 1:0..1 cascade | Via `owns_trip` |
| `ai_generations` | One row per generation attempt | MOD-B06 | `provider`, `model_id`, prompt, schema and adapter versions; `scope`, `scope_day_number`; `status`, `outcome`, `failure_reason`; repair counts; `validation_summary`; latency and tokens; `request_hash`; `retention_until` | trip 1:N cascade; profile 1:N cascade | `user_id`; browser read only |
| `itinerary_days` | Days of the current plan | MOD-B08 | `day_number` unique per trip, `plan_date`, `theme`; EXT (0008): `explanation` (≤ 400 chars, AI-written), `explanation_revision`, `explanation_generated_at`, all set or all null | trip 1:N cascade; source generation set null | Via `owns_trip`; browser read only |
| `itinerary_items` | Activities of the current plan | MOD-B08 | `position` (unique per day, deferrable), `place_id`, `slot_type`, `start_time`, `duration_min`, `origin`, `note`/`note_origin`, `is_locked`, `cost_*`, `travel_*` | day 1:N cascade via (`day_id`, `trip_id`); trip cascade; place restrict | Via `owns_trip`; browser read only |
| `itinerary_warnings` | Findings of the latest validation | MOD-B08 (content from MOD-B07) | `plan_revision`, `code` (13 codes), `severity`, `message`, `day_number`, `item_id`, `place_id` (MUST_VISIT_MISSING only, IMD-42), `suggested_fix` | trip 1:N cascade; item 0..1:N cascade | Via `owns_trip`; browser read only |
| `itinerary_versions` | Read-only plan snapshots | MOD-B08 | `version_no` unique per trip, `reason`, `name` (unique per trip when set), `plan_revision`, `snapshot`, `validation_summary` | trip 1:N cascade; generation and creator set null | Via `owns_trip`; browser read only |
| `route_cache` | Travel times between place pairs | MOD-B10 | PK (`from_place_id`, `to_place_id`, `mode`); `travel_minutes`, `distance_m`, `travel_source`, `expires_at` | places cascade | Shared; no browser access |
| `checklist_items` (EXT, 0007) | Packing list items | MOD-B12 | `kind` (only `packing` in EXT), `label` 1 to 160, `category`, `origin` rule, ai or user, `status` active, suggested or rejected, `is_checked`, `sort_order`; one rule item per label and trip (`ux_checklist_rule_label`) | trip 1:N cascade | Via `owns_trip`; browser read only |
| `ai_assist_calls` (EXT, 0007) | One row per assist call (trip intake, day explanation, packing refinement) | MOD-B05 (`app/ai/assist_log.py`) | `purpose`, `provider`, `model_id`, `prompt_template_id`, `prompt_version`, `status` ok, rejected or failed, `failure_reason`, latency and tokens, `retention_until`; no prompt or output text | profile 1:N cascade; trip 0..1:N cascade (null only for `trip_intake`) | `user_id`; browser read only |
| `weather_cache` (EXT, 0009) | Daily forecast per destination | MOD-B16 | PK (`destination_id`, `forecast_date`); `precip_probability_max` 0 to 100, `precipitation_sum`, `weather_code`, `temp_max`/`temp_min`, `fetched_at` | destination 1:N cascade | Shared; RLS on, no policy, no browser access |
| `context_cards` (EXT, 0010) | Cached Wikivoyage or Wikipedia extracts | MOD-B17 | `subject_type` place or destination, `subject_id`, `source`, `page_title`, `extract` ≤ 1,200 chars, `page_url` (wiki URL check), `licence` (CC BY-SA 4.0), `retrieved_at`, `expires_at`; unique (`subject_type`, `subject_id`, `source`) | none (subject checked by the service) | Shared; RLS on, no policy, no browser access |

Enumerated values are stored exactly as the API returns them. `travel_source` is `routing_api` or `fallback_estimate`. `price_label`, `hours_label` and `cost_label` are `curated`, `estimate` or `unavailable`. `verification_status` is `unverified`, `curated_checked`, `imported_osm` or `estimated`. Status, outcome, failure-reason, provider and finding-code values are those of §3 and §8.

**Snapshot format.** `itinerary_versions.snapshot` holds `{"schema": "snap-1", "plan_revision": n, "days": [{"day_number", "plan_date", "theme", "items": [{"place_id", "position", "slot_type", "start_time", "duration_min", "origin", "note", "note_origin", "is_locked"}]}], "budget_settings": {...}}` (Provisional, IMD-18). A restore writes these rows back and recalculates costs, travel times and findings through the edit transaction (§5.8). Costs are never copied from a snapshot. Reading a version (API-24 with `version_id`) runs the budget engine and validator over the snapshot on read and writes nothing (IMD-18).

## 5.3 Constraints and indexes

Exact definitions are in Appendix A. The rules below matter to application code, which must map their violations to the error envelope of §6 and never let a database error reach the client as text.

| Rule | Mechanism | Error to the client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trip of 1 to 14 days; end not before start; budget amount and currency both set or both null | CHECK on the generated `num_days`; CHECK | Validated first in Pydantic, so a 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR` is returned before the database sees it |
| Item position unique per day; swaps allowed inside one transaction | `unique (day_id, position) deferrable initially deferred` | None; the edit service writes all positions in one transaction |
| An item belongs to the same trip as its day | Composite FK (`day_id`, `trip_id`) | None (internal invariant) |
| Status, outcome, completion time and failure reason are paired; `scope_day_number` is set exactly when `scope = 'day'` | CHECK on `ai_generations` | None (internal invariant; a violation is a 500 bug) |
| Price range needs a currency; max not below min; curated hours carry a check date | CHECK on `places` | Seed rejects the row and reports it (§5.6) |
| Travel minutes, mode and source are set together; a note has an origin | CHECK on `itinerary_items` | None (internal invariant) |
| One relation per place per trip | UNIQUE (`trip_id`, `place_id`) | The service updates the relation; repeated PUTs are idempotent |
| Version name unique per trip; a `manual` version has a name | Partial UNIQUE `ux_versions_name`; CHECK | 409 `CONFLICT` |
| Re-import creates no duplicates | Partial UNIQUE (`source_id`, `external_ref`) | Upsert (§5.6) |
| Money exact | `numeric` columns with a currency code | n/a; the API returns two-decimal strings (IMD-05) |
| EXT: only AI items can be `suggested` or `rejected`; only `active` items can be ticked; one rule item per label | CHECKs on `checklist_items`; partial UNIQUE `ux_checklist_rule_label` | Ticking a suggested or rejected item → 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (checked in the service first); rule items are inserted with `on conflict do nothing` |
| EXT: an assist call has a trip unless it is a trip intake; `failure_reason` null on ok calls, an error class on failed calls, `invalid_output` on rejected calls | CHECKs on `ai_assist_calls` | None (internal invariant) |
| EXT: explanation, its revision and its time are set together | CHECK `ck_days_explanation_complete` | None (internal invariant) |
| EXT: context page URL is a Wikivoyage or Wikipedia HTTPS URL; extract ≤ 1,200 characters | CHECKs on `context_cards` | None; the refresh job skips and logs a page that fails them |

Indexes in Appendix A serve these queries: the dashboard (`ix_trips_user`), the purge (`ix_trips_purge`, `ix_aigen_retention`), daily quota and active-job checks (`ix_aigen_user_day`, `ix_aigen_active`, `ix_aigen_trip`), place search (`ix_places_dest_cat`, GIN `ix_places_tags`), current findings (`ix_warnings_trip`) and cache refresh (`ix_route_cache_expiry`). The extension indexes serve the packing list (`ix_checklist_items_trip`), the daily assist cap and purge (`ix_assist_user_day`, `ix_assist_retention`) and cache refresh (`ix_weather_fetched`, `ix_context_expires`). Add any further index only after `EXPLAIN` on realistic data shows a need, and add it as a new migration.

## 5.4 Ownership and access control

| Rule | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Lock 1: API authorization (the one the MVP relies on) | Every repository function of an owned table takes `user_id` from `CurrentUser` (§3, IMD-04) and filters by it (for example `trips.user_id = :user_id and deleted_at is null`). Child rows are reached only through an owned trip. A missing or foreign resource returns 404 `NOT_FOUND`, identical in both cases. |
| Lock 2: row-level security | Enabled on all 15 MVP tables (migration 0005) and on the four extension tables in the migration that creates them (0007, 0009, 0010). Reference tables are readable by `authenticated`. Owned tables use `user_id = auth.uid()` or `app_private.owns_trip(trip_id)`; `checklist_items` uses `owns_trip` and `ai_assist_calls` uses `user_id`, both select-only. Plan tables are select-only for owners. `route_cache`, `weather_cache` and `context_cards` have no policy. |
| Lock 3: no browser privileges | Migration 0005 revokes all table privileges from `anon` and `authenticated`. Migration 0006 revokes the helper functions and `alembic_version` (IMD-19). Migrations 0007, 0009 and 0010 revoke all privileges on the tables they create. The browser uses Supabase only for sign-in and never queries a table. |
| Backend connection | `DATABASE_URL` is a privileged role held as a backend secret. Whether that role bypasses RLS on hosted Supabase is Awaiting validation (blueprint §16.8). The two-user suite (`tests/authz`) tests Lock 1 through the API either way. |
| Profile creation | On the first authenticated request, the `CurrentUser` dependency calls `get_or_create_profile` in `auth/service.py`, which inserts `profiles(id)` with `on conflict do nothing` (IMD-14). No endpoint calls it separately and no trigger is placed on the `auth` schema. |
| Model output | The model never receives database access. Its place IDs are validated against `places` before any write (§8), and all writes are parameterised SQLAlchemy statements. |

## 5.5 Migrations

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Files | `apps/api/migrations/sql/000N_<name>.sql` (up) and `apps/api/migrations/sql/down/000N_<name>.down.sql` (down) hold the SQL of Appendix A. `apps/api/migrations/versions/000N_<name>.py` has `revision = "000N"`, `down_revision = "000(N-1)"` (None for 0001), and runs `op.execute(<file text>)` in `upgrade()` and the down file in `downgrade()`. No autogenerate. |
| Driver | `postgresql+psycopg://` for both Alembic (synchronous) and the application (asynchronous engine). `migrations/env.py` reads `DATABASE_URL` from the settings object, never from `alembic.ini`. |
| Commands | `make db-migrate` (`alembic upgrade head`). Inspect with `alembic current` and `alembic heads` run from `apps/api`. A new migration is `alembic revision -m "<description>"` plus its two SQL files. |
| One head | `alembic heads` must print exactly one revision. CI fails on more. The integration lead (Kirtan) resolves head conflicts. One migration per pull request, together with its ORM-model change. |
| Never edit a merged migration | Changes are new revisions that add first and remove in a later release. Destructive downgrades are for local and staging only. Production is never downgraded; it is restored from the pre-release export (§14). |
| CI | The API job starts PostgreSQL 16 (compose service `db`), applies `test_auth_stub.sql`, runs `alembic upgrade head` on the blank database, then `alembic downgrade base` and `upgrade head` again (round-trip check), then the suites. |
| ORM mirror and drift test | `app/db/models/<owner>.py` declares the same tables for queries only. `tests/api/test_schema_drift.py` reflects the migrated test database and compares every table, column, type, nullability and server default with the ORM metadata, failing on any difference. `Base.metadata.create_all` is never used. |
| Extension migrations (EXT) | `0007_packing_and_assist` (IMP-613, Sprint 6), `0008_day_explanations` (IMP-709, Sprint 7), `0009_weather_cache` (IMP-710, Sprint 7) and `0010_context_cards` (IMP-713, Sprint 7), each in its own pull request with its ORM change (IMD-36). Revision numbers are fixed, but the pull requests may merge in any order inside the extension sprints: the one that merges later rebases and sets its `down_revision` to the current head, so `alembic heads` still prints one revision. An extension that is switched off keeps its migration (an empty table costs nothing); one that is never started has no migration. The one shared table, `ai_assist_calls`, is created by 0007; if IMP-613 is cut before it starts, IMP-708 or IMP-709, whichever starts first, creates the `ai_assist_calls` part of 0007 as `0011_assist_calls`; 0007 is then never written and its number stays unused (IMD-60). |
| Later releases | T1 tables arrive in migration `0101_tier1_tables` and R2 tables in `0201_release2_tables`. Neither is written before its release starts (blueprint §30.5). `checklist_items` is now created by 0007; `0101` adds only the other checklist kinds when T1 starts. |

## 5.6 Seed data

`python -m app.places.seed <dir> [<dir> ...]` (`make seed`; extra directories through `SEED_DIRS`) loads one destination per directory through the import pipeline and quality gate (IMP-107 minimal, IMP-205 complete). It is the only writer of the four reference tables.

| File (per destination directory) | Columns or keys | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destination.json` | `slug`, `name`, `region`, `country_code`, `timezone` (IANA), `currency`, `center` {`lat`, `lon`}, `bbox` {`min_lat`, `max_lat`, `min_lon`, `max_lon`}, `is_sample` | Upsert by `slug`. The time zone is checked with `zoneinfo`. |
| `sources.csv` | `name`, `source_type`, `licence`, `attribution_text`, `url`, `retrieved_on` (YYYY-MM-DD), `notes` | Upsert by `name`. Every place must cite one of these names. |
| `places.csv` | `external_ref` (required), `source_name`, `name`, `category`, `tags` (`;`-separated), `description`, `address`, `lat`, `lon`, `typical_duration_min`, `price_min`, `price_max`, `price_currency`, `price_label`, `hours_label`, `hours_checked_on`, `verification_status`, `step_free`, `child_friendly`, `indoor` (`true`, `false` or empty for unknown), `website_url`, `booking_url` | Upsert by (`source_id`, `external_ref`). Places of the same source that are missing from the file are set `is_active = false`, never deleted. |
| `opening_hours.csv` | `external_ref`, `weekday` (1 = Monday), `is_closed`, `open_time` (HH:MM), `close_time`, `closes_next_day` | Replaced as a set per place. A place without rows gets `hours_label = unavailable`. |

| Quality gate (FR-022, FR-023) | If it fails |
| --- | --- |
| Row names a known source and a verification status; `external_ref` present | Row rejected and listed |
| Coordinates inside the destination bounding box | Row rejected |
| Hours parse into weekday intervals | Hours stored as unavailable; row flagged |
| Prices: not negative; max not below min; a range has a currency; `price_label` not `unavailable` when a price is given | Row rejected |
| Category in the allowed list; duration 15 to 480 minutes | Row rejected |
| Destination has at least the minimum usable places (fixture 30; curated about 100, AS-06) | Shortfall line in the report; the seed still exits 0 |

The seed writes everything in one transaction per destination, in the order data_sources, destinations, places, opening_hours. It prints a report of rows read, loaded, updated, deactivated and rejected (with reasons), and for `data/places/<slug>/` writes the same report to `quality_report.md` beside the data. A second run with unchanged files changes nothing (`tests/api/test_seed.py`).

**Sample and curated data.** `data/fixtures/sampleton/` is synthetic. `is_sample = true`, a source named "SAMPLE fixture data" (`source_type = other`, `notes = synthetic`), places with `verification_status = estimated` and price and hours labels `estimate`. The API returns `is_sample`, and the web app shows a "Sample data" label on any trip for that destination. The seed refuses any `destination.json` with `is_sample = true` unless `APP_ENV` is `local` or `test`, so staging and production hold only curated destinations. Curated data under `data/places/<slug>/` is entered by people from the named public pages, never from memory or from a model (blueprint §30.5). Nothing is labelled live or verified in the MVP.

**Test data.** Automated tests use only the fixture destination plus factories in `tests/fixtures/factories.py`. Those factories create `auth.users` rows on the stubbed database, then profiles, trips, preferences and itineraries with fixed UUIDs, so test runs are repeatable.

## 5.7 Reset and lifecycle

`make db-reset` refuses to run unless `APP_ENV` is `local` or `test` and the host of `DATABASE_URL` is `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`.

- **Compose database (port 5432):** it drops and recreates the database named in the URL, applies the auth stub, then runs `db-migrate` and `seed`.
- **Supabase local stack (port 54322):** it runs `supabase db reset`, then `db-migrate` and `seed`.
- **Staging and production:** never reset. Data fixes go through a reviewed migration or the seed.

| Event | Effect | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trip deleted (API-12) | `deleted_at` set. The trip disappears from every route and from RLS. | Soft delete |
| 30 days after `deleted_at` (Proposed, OD-10) | Trip removed; children go by cascade | Daily purge job in `generation/jobs.py`, same scheduler as the reaper (IMD-31; built in IMP-602) |
| `retention_until` reached (90 days, Proposed) | `ai_generations` row deleted; `source_generation_id` and `generation_id` become null | Daily purge (IMD-31; built in IMP-511) |
| Automatic versions beyond the newest 20 per trip (IMD-18) | Oldest automatic versions deleted. Named (`manual`) versions are kept. | Version service after each insert |
| Trip archived or unarchived (API-11) | `status` set to `archived`. On unarchive it returns to `ready` if the trip has days, otherwise `draft`. | Trip service |
| Place retired | `is_active = false`; plans that refer to it stay readable | Seed |
| Account deletion | R2 (FR-006): cascade from `auth.users`. Until then, deletion on a verified request is an operator procedure (NFR-022). | Not built in the MVP |
| Route-cache expiry (30 days) | Pair recomputed on next use | Routing service |
| EXT: trip deleted or purged | `checklist_items` and the trip's `ai_assist_calls` go with the trip by cascade | Purge job |
| EXT: `ai_assist_calls.retention_until` reached (90 days, Proposed) | Row deleted | Daily purge, which calls `assist_log.purge_expired()` so that MOD-B05 stays the one writer (IMP-613) |
| EXT: plan edited after a day explanation was written | The explanation stays stored but is reported out of date (`explanation_revision` ≠ `trips.plan_revision`) until API-65 refreshes it; a generation that rewrites the day deletes and reinserts the row, which clears it | Itinerary service |
| EXT: weather row older than 3 hours | Refetched for the destination on the next API-68 call; rows for dates before today are deleted by the daily purge | Weather service |
| EXT: context card past `expires_at` (30 days) | Refreshed by the background job; on a failed refresh the old card is kept until it expires and is then deleted, so no card is shown | Context job in the scheduler of `generation/jobs.py` |

## 5.8 Transaction boundaries

Each row is one database transaction, opened by the owning service through `app/db/session.py` (`async with session.begin()`). No transaction stays open across a provider call.

| Operation | Inside one transaction | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create trip (API-07) | Insert `trips` (draft) and `budget_settings` with defaults; no `trip_preferences` row (API-14 creates it, IMD-25; the wizard pre-fills from `profiles.default_preferences`) | Profile already ensured by `CurrentUser` (IMD-14) |
| Save preferences (API-14) | Upsert `trip_preferences`; replace `must_visit` rows of `trip_places`; set `trips.plan_stale = true` if a plan exists | |
| Start generation (API-22, API-30, API-31) | `select ... for update` on the trip; active-job check; cap check; insert `ai_generations` (queued); for API-30 and API-31 also insert a snapshot of the current plan (`regeneration`, always; when the versions switch is off it replaces the single backup copy, IMD-18) | The task starts after commit. Status updates later are separate short transactions. |
| Save generation result (pipeline step 11) | Lock the trip; check that `plan_revision` is unchanged since the job started (otherwise fail with `internal` and keep the newer plan; a safety net, because edits are refused during a job, IMD-23); delete and insert `itinerary_days` and `itinerary_items` (for day scope, only that day); replace `itinerary_warnings`; insert `itinerary_versions`; increment `trips.plan_revision`; set `status = ready`, `plan_stale = false`; complete the `ai_generations` row | A crash leaves the old plan or the new one (NFR-008) |
| Edit an item (API-25 to API-29) | Lock the trip; refuse with 409 `GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` if a generation for the trip is active (IMD-23); compare `plan_revision` (409 `STALE_PLAN` on mismatch); apply the operation; renumber positions; recompute travel and costs; revalidate; replace warnings; insert an automatic version (`edit`, IMD-18); increment `plan_revision` | Travel times are read from `route_cache` or estimated. A routing call, if needed, is made before the transaction opens. |
| Save a named version (API-37) | Lock the trip; refuse while a generation is active (IMD-23); insert `itinerary_versions` (`manual`, `name`, next `version_no`) | 409 `CONFLICT` on a duplicate name (IMD-18) |
| Restore a version (API-38) | Lock the trip; refuse while a generation is active (IMD-23); check revision; insert an automatic version of the current plan (`restore`); rewrite days and items from the snapshot; recalculate; revalidate; increment revision | |
| Duplicate trip (API-13) | Insert a new trip (draft or ready), preferences, budget settings, trip_places, days and items (re-validated); `plan_revision` 1 if a plan was copied; versions and generations are not copied | |
| Budget settings (API-34) | Upsert `budget_settings` | Returns the recalculated cost estimate with its budget findings (computed, as for API-33); `itinerary_warnings` is not written |
| EXT: Apply an optimised order (API-67) | Exactly the edit transaction above, with the operation "write the new positions and start times of the day's unlocked items"; the `item_ids` sent must be the day's items in an order where locked items and meal slots keep their positions, else 422 `INVALID_EDIT`; a changed plan is caught by the `plan_revision` check | The travel-time matrix is read or fetched before the transaction opens |
| EXT: Swap two days (API-69) | Exactly the edit transaction above, with the operation "exchange the items of `day_a` and `day_b`, keeping each day's `plan_date`"; any locked item on either day → 422 `INVALID_EDIT` and nothing changes | Day explanations of both days become out of date |
| EXT: Save a day explanation (API-65) | Provider call first, outside any transaction; then lock the trip, refuse while a generation is active (IMD-23), check that `plan_revision` is unchanged since the call started (else store nothing and return 409 `STALE_PLAN`), update the three explanation columns of that day | `plan_revision` is not incremented and no version is written: the explanation is not part of the plan. The `ai_assist_calls` row is written in its own short transaction whatever the outcome |
| EXT: First read of the packing list (API-43) | When the trip has no packing items yet, insert the rule items with `on conflict do nothing` on `ux_checklist_rule_label`; then read | Repeated or concurrent first reads create no duplicates |
| EXT: Refine the packing list (API-74) | Provider call first, outside any transaction; then insert the accepted vocabulary items as `origin ai`, `status suggested` | Rule and user items are never changed. Assist log as for API-65 |
| EXT: Update a packing item (API-75) | Update one `checklist_items` row of the owned trip | |
| EXT: Weather and context caches | Upsert per destination (weather) or per subject and source (context) in one short transaction after the HTTP call | No HTTP call is made inside a transaction |

The rows marked EXT cover the extension endpoints of §6.6.7 and were checked against migrations 0007 to 0010.

Note 1. The blueprint's examples show an item price as `{amount, label}`, but the schema stores a range. Under IMD-05 and IMD-20 the API exposes `price` as `{"min", "max", "currency", "label"}`, with two-decimal strings and nulls when unavailable. §6 must use this shape. The same rule applies to place prices.

# 6. Canonical API contract

This section is the only definition of the HTTP interface. The 36 MVP endpoints keep their blueprint IDs (API-01 to API-38, without API-05 and API-18). The extension release (EXT, Sprints 5 to 7) adds 14 endpoints, each behind a switch: API-43 (promoted from T1) and the new API-63 to API-75 (§6.6.7). FastAPI generates the OpenAPI document from the Pydantic models named here; `make openapi` writes it to `contracts/openapi.v1.json` and regenerates the web types (IMD-06). If this section and the generated document disagree, the generated document is wrong and the pull request is not merged. Field names equal the column names of Appendix A unless the "DB source" column says how a field is derived.

## 6.1 Conventions

| Topic | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Base path and versioning | Resources under `/api/v1`; health at `/health` and `/health/ready` (no version). Adding an optional response field is allowed inside v1; removing, renaming or retyping a field needs `/api/v2` (no v2 is planned) |
| Format | JSON, UTF-8. Request models reject unknown fields with 422 (`extra="forbid"`); clients ignore unknown response fields |
| Identifiers | UUID strings (lower case, hyphenated) for every resource; `day_number` is an integer 1 to 14 |
| Dates and times | Dates `YYYY-MM-DD` (calendar dates at the destination, DR-01); times of day `HH:MM` local to the destination, no offset (DR-02); timestamps ISO 8601 UTC with `Z`; durations whole minutes |
| Money (IMD-05) | A money value is a JSON string with exactly two decimals, `"1230.00"`, next to a `currency` field (ISO 4217). Ranges are objects `{ "min": "…", "max": "…", "currency": "INR" }`. The backend computes in integer minor units (DR-20) and formats at the edge; the web app formats and never adds amounts |
| Labels | `price_label`, `hours_label`, `cost_label` are `curated`, `estimate` or `unavailable`; `travel_source` is `routing_api` or `fallback_estimate` (DDL values) |
| Pagination | Only API-08 and API-16: query `limit` (default 20, 1 to 50) and `offset` (default 0); response `Page<T>` = `items`, `total`, `limit`, `offset`. All other lists are bounded by design (at most 14 days, 3 alternatives, a trip's versions) |
| Idempotency | API-22, API-30, API-31 use `request_hash` (§6.4). API-19 and API-20 are idempotent by definition. No `Idempotency-Key` header is implemented in the MVP |
| Concurrency | Every itinerary response carries `plan_revision`. Every edit, regeneration, restore and named-version request sends the `plan_revision` it was based on; a mismatch returns 409 `STALE_PLAN` and changes nothing (FR-069) |
| Rate limiting | Per user (and per client address for unauthenticated routes): `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN` (Proposed 60) on API-16, API-22, API-25 to API-31 and the extension routes API-64, API-65, API-67, API-69 and API-74; 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` header and `retry_after_s` (FR-126). Daily generation caps are separate (`AI_QUOTA_REACHED`, §6.4) |
| CORS | Allowed origins exactly `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`; methods GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE; headers `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `X-Request-ID`; credentials not used (bearer token) |
| Request ID | Every response has `X-Request-ID`; a client-supplied UUID is kept, otherwise generated. It appears in each log line and in the error envelope (FR-125). Prompt text, keys and tokens are never logged |
| OpenAPI page | `/docs` enabled when `APP_ENV` is local, test or staging; disabled in production |

## 6.2 Authentication and ownership

| Class | Endpoints | Token | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | API-01, API-02 | none | Return no user data and no configuration values except provider name and model identifier |
| Reference data | API-06, API-16, API-17; EXT: API-72, API-73 | required | Shared read-only rows; inactive destinations and places are invisible (404) |
| Own resources | all other MVP and EXT endpoints | required | The trip, or the item, generation or version under it, must belong to the token's user and the trip must not be soft-deleted; otherwise 404 `NOT_FOUND`, identical to a missing resource (FR-005, NFR-012) |

The `CurrentUser` dependency (`app/auth/deps.py`, IMP-108) verifies `Authorization: Bearer <token>` per IMD-04 (JWKS when `SUPABASE_JWKS_URL` is set, otherwise HS256 with `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`; audience `authenticated`; `exp` checked) and yields `user_id` (claim `sub`) and `email`. No endpoint accepts a user ID in a path, query or body; a body field naming a user is rejected by `extra="forbid"` (FR-003 AC2, IMD-45). Repositories take `user_id` as a required argument and filter by it. The dependency itself calls `get_or_create_profile(user_id)` in `auth/service.py`, which inserts the `profiles` row if absent (insert … on conflict do nothing), because `trips.user_id` references `profiles.id` (IMD-14); no endpoint calls it separately. A body that names a user (for example `user_id`) is rejected with 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR` (IMD-45). An archived trip (`status = archived`) is read-only: every write under it except API-11 (to unarchive), API-12 and API-13 returns 409 `CONFLICT` (FR-015 AC3).

## 6.3 Error envelope and codes

Every non-2xx response has this body; `message` is safe to show; `details` lists field problems (`field`, `message`) or is empty; nothing else (no stack trace, SQL, key or prompt) is returned.

```json
{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Some fields need attention.",
  "request_id": "0b7e2c94-5d1a-4c3f-8a60-9e4d1f2b7c35",
  "details": [ { "field": "end_date", "message": "End date must be on or after start date." } ],
  "retry_after_s": null } }
```

| HTTP | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Token missing, malformed, expired or unverifiable |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Resource missing, not owned, soft-deleted, inactive, or the route belongs to a feature switched off by `FEATURES_DISABLED` (IMD-11) |
| 409 | `STALE_PLAN` | `plan_revision` in the request is not the stored one |
| 409 | `GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` | A different generation for the trip is queued, running, validating or repairing; also any edit, replace, version save or restore on that trip while it is active (IMD-23) |
| 409 | `CONFLICT` | Other state conflicts: trip archived (read-only, IMD-35), itinerary already exists (use API-31, IMD-21), no itinerary yet (API-30/31/37), version name taken |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Body, path or query fails the schema or a field rule; `details` names the fields |
| 422 | `INVALID_EDIT` | Structurally impossible edit: day out of range, position out of range, unknown or inactive place, moving or retiming a locked item |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Request rate exceeded; `retry_after_s` set |
| 429 | `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` | Daily per-user or global AI generation cap reached (FR-046); `details` = `[{ "field": "scope", "message": "user" or "global" }]`, `retry_after_s` = seconds to the next 00:00 UTC. EXT: the daily per-user assist cap `AI_DAILY_ASSIST_CALLS_PER_USER` on API-64, API-65 and API-74 uses the same code with scope `assist` |
| 500 | `INTERNAL` | Unexpected fault; logged with the request ID |
| 501 | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` | Temporary: the endpoint is declared in the contract but its handler is not built yet (IMD-37). MVP routes: Sprints 2 to 6 only, SG-6 requires that none returns it. Extension routes (API-43, API-63 to API-75): from the day their card declares them until SG-7, where each is built or switched off (404) |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | Database unreachable |

Every protected endpoint can also return 401, 429 `RATE_LIMITED` (where limited), 500 and 503; these are not repeated in §6.6. Provider failures are never HTTP errors: they end in the rule-based fallback or in a `failed` generation (§6.4). Implementation: domain exceptions in `app/core/errors.py`, one exception handler per class, FastAPI's `RequestValidationError` mapped to `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `details` (IMP-103).

## 6.4 Asynchronous generation lifecycle

Initial generation (API-22), whole regeneration (API-31) and day regeneration (API-30) all create one `ai_generations` row and run as an in-process task (IMD-12). The browser polls API-23.

::: {custom-style="Figure"}
*Figure: Generation status lifecycle (API-22, API-30, API-31 create; API-23 reads). (Diagram in the PDF edition.)*
:::

::: {custom-style="Caption"}
Figure 10. Generation status lifecycle (API-22, API-30, API-31 create; API-23 reads)
:::

| Step | Server rule | Client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create | Checks in order: trip owned and not archived; trip complete (title, destination, dates, adults, a `trip_preferences` row; else 422 listing missing fields, FR-024 AC2); API-22 only: no current itinerary (else 409 `CONFLICT`); API-30/31: `plan_revision` current (else 409 `STALE_PLAN`); `mode = ai` only: `profiles.ai_notice_ack_at` set (else 422, field `ai_notice`), daily caps (else 429 `AI_QUOTA_REACHED`). Computes `request_hash` = SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `{trip_id, scope, day_number, mode, plan_revision}`. If an active generation exists for the trip: same hash → 200 with that generation (FR-024 AC3); different hash → 409 `GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS`. Otherwise inserts the row (`status queued`; `provider` and `model_id` of the active provider, or `model_id = rule_based_planner_v1` with the configured provider name when `mode = rule_based`) and returns 202 | Show GenerationProgress; start polling |
| Poll | API-23 returns the row. If the row is active and older than 150 s, the reaper marks it `failed` / `internal` before answering | Poll every 2 s, back off to 5 s; stop on `completed` or `failed`; after 160 s without a terminal status show "connection problem" with Reload |
| Complete | One transaction writes days, items, warnings, a version (`reason` generation, regeneration or fallback), increments `trips.plan_revision`, clears `plan_stale`, sets `status completed`, `outcome`, `completed_at` (NFR-008) | Read API-24; show FallbackNotice when `outcome = fallback_rule_based`, "some details were adjusted" when `model_repaired` |
| Validation failure | Error findings → deterministic repair, then at most one model retry (`repair_attempts` ≤ 1), then rule-based plan; only if the rule-based plan is also unusable: `failed` / `unresolved_validation` | As Fail |
| Timeout | Provider call timeout is handled inside the pipeline (fallback). The whole pipeline is cancelled after 120 s (NFR-004) and marked `failed`; the reaper catches jobs whose process died | As Fail |
| Fail | `status failed`, `outcome failed`, `failure_reason` set; the plan and trip are unchanged (FR-037 AC3) | Show ErrorState with `failure_message` and the `next_action` button |
| Retry | No server-side retry endpoint: the client starts a new generation (same endpoint). `mode = rule_based` is always offered after a failure or `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` (FR-046 AC2); rule-based runs are not counted against the AI caps | Offer "Try again" and "Build a plan without AI" |
| Cancel | Not supported in the MVP; no endpoint exists. A cancel route would be Release 2 | Leaving the page does not stop the job |

`failure_reason` (DDL values) maps to the user-facing `failure_message` and `next_action` that API-23 adds: `provider_timeout`, `provider_rate_limited`, `provider_unavailable`, `invalid_output` → "The AI service did not return a usable plan." / `retry_rule_based`; `provider_quota_exhausted` → "AI generation is paused for today." / `retry_rule_based` (FR-037 AC2); `unresolved_validation` → "No plan satisfied the checks; adjust the trip or must-visit places." / `edit_trip`; `config_error` → "The AI service is not available right now." / `retry_rule_based`; `internal` → "Something went wrong on our side." / `retry`. The 120-second hard timeout and the reaper record `internal` with message "Generation timed out." (IMD-22); quota exhaustion ends `failed` with a one-click rule-based generation (blueprint §19.2.2).

## 6.5 Shared schemas

Field tables list response fields; input models (`…In`) are the writable subset marked "in". Types: `uuid`, `date`, `time` (`HH:MM`), `ts` (UTC timestamp), `money` (IMD-05 string), `int`, `bool`, `str`, `enum`.

**TripIn / TripPatch / TripOut** (`trips`, `app/trips/schemas.py`)

| Field | Type | In | Rule | DB source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | uuid | – | | `id` |
| title | str | create, patch | 1 to 120 chars, trimmed | `title` |
| destination_id | uuid | create, patch | active destination, else 422 with the supported list in `details` (FR-007 AC2) | `destination_id` |
| start_date, end_date | date | create, patch | end ≥ start; 1 to 14 days (FR-008) | same |
| num_days | int | – | end − start + 1 | generated column |
| adults, children | int | create, patch | 1 to 20; 0 to 20 | same |
| group_needs | enum[] | create, patch | subset of `children`, `older_adults`, `reduced_mobility` (Provisional list) | `group_needs` |
| budget | object or null | create, patch | `{amount: money > 0, currency: ISO 4217}`; both or neither (DR-16, DR-17); group total | `budget_amount`, `budget_currency` |
| status | enum | patch | `draft`, `ready`, `archived`; patch may set `archived` or (from archived) `ready`; `ready` is otherwise set by API-14 (IMD-25) | `status` |
| plan_revision | int | – | | `plan_revision` |
| plan_stale | bool | – | true after dates, travellers, destination, budget or preferences change while an itinerary exists (FR-011) | `plan_stale` |
| has_itinerary | bool | – | any `itinerary_days` row | derived |
| destination | object | – | `{id, name, timezone, currency, is_sample}` | join `destinations` |
| created_at, updated_at | ts | – | | same |

**PreferencesIn / PreferencesOut** (`trip_preferences`, `trip_places` relation `must_visit`)

| Field | Type | Rule | DB source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| interests | enum[] | subset of place categories except `stay` | `interests` |
| pace | enum | `relaxed`, `balanced`, `busy` | `pace` |
| budget_priority | enum | `saving`, `balanced`, `comfort` | `budget_priority` |
| transport_pref | enum | `walking`, `local_transport`, `car` | `transport_pref` |
| accommodation_type | enum | `budget`, `mid_range`, `premium`, `any` | `accommodation_type` |
| step_free_required | bool | | `step_free_required` |
| notes | str or null | ≤ 1,000 chars; control characters removed; sent to the model only as quoted data (FR-026 AC2) | `notes` |
| must_visit_place_ids | uuid[] | ≤ 10 (Provisional); active places of the trip's destination, else 422 | `trip_places` |
| effects (out only) | object[] | `{field, effect: filter \| rank \| note}` per field (FR-009 AC3) | mapping table in `trips/preference_mapping.py` (version `pm-1`, IMD-29) |

**PlaceSummary / PlaceOut** (`places`, `place_opening_hours`, `data_sources`)

| Field | Type | Rule | DB source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id, name, category, tags | uuid, str, enum, str[] | | same |
| lat, lon | number | 6 decimals | same |
| typical_duration_min | int | | same |
| price | object or null | `{min, max, currency, label}`; null when no price | `price_min`, `price_max`, `price_currency`, `price_label` |
| price_label, hours_label | enum | always present | same |
| verification_status | enum | `unverified`, `curated_checked`, `imported_osm`, `estimated` | same |
| suitability | object | `{step_free, child_friendly, indoor}`, each true, false or null (unknown, FR-019 AC2) | same |
| distance_m (summary, optional) | int | only when `near_lat`/`near_lon` given | derived |
| description, address, website_url, booking_url (detail) | str or null | | same |
| hours (detail) | object[] | `{weekday 1-7, is_closed, open_time, close_time, closes_next_day}` | `place_opening_hours` |
| hours_checked_on (detail) | date or null | | same |
| source (detail) | object | `{name, source_type, licence, attribution_text, url, retrieved_on}` | `data_sources` |
| saved, must_visit (when `trip_id` given) | bool | relation on that trip | `trip_places` |

**GenerationOut** (`ai_generations`)

| Field | Type | Rule | DB source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id, trip_id | uuid | | same |
| scope | enum | `full`, `day` | `scope` |
| day_number | int or null | for `day` | `scope_day_number` |
| mode | enum | `ai`, `rule_based` | derived: `model_id = rule_based_planner_v1` |
| status, outcome, failure_reason | enum | §6.4 | same |
| failure_message, next_action | str, enum | §6.4 mapping | derived |
| fallback_reason | enum or null | on `completed` with outcome `fallback_rule_based`: the provider failure that caused the fallback (same values as `failure_reason`; IMD-22) | `validation_summary.provider_failure` |
| provider, model_id, prompt_version | str | names only | same |
| repair_attempts, deterministic_repairs | int | | same |
| validation_summary | object | `{errors, warnings, infos}` counts | same |
| latency_ms | int or null | | same |
| itinerary_version_id | uuid or null | set on `completed` | `itinerary_versions.generation_id` |
| plan_revision | int or null | set on `completed` | `itinerary_versions.plan_revision` |
| created_at, completed_at | ts | | same |

**ItineraryOut, Day, Item, Finding, Totals** (`itinerary_days`, `itinerary_items`, `itinerary_warnings`)

| Schema | Fields (DB source) |
| --- | --- |
| ItineraryOut | `trip_id`; `plan_revision` (`trips`); `version_id` (latest version); `is_current` (false when read with `version_id`); `plan_stale`; `source` `{generation_id, provider, outcome}` (latest completed generation); `days[]`; `findings[]` (warnings of the current revision); `totals` |
| Day | `day_number`; `date` (`plan_date`); EXT only, while `day_explain` is enabled: `explanation`, `explanation_origin`, `explanation_current`, `explanation_generated_at` (below); `theme` (**ai_written** when `theme_origin = ai`) and `theme_origin` (`ai` when the source generation outcome is `model` or `model_repaired`, else `none`); `items[]` ordered by `position`; `day_cost` `{min, max, currency, complete}` |
| Item | `id`; `position`; `place` `{id, name, category, lat, lon, hours_label}`; `slot_type` (`activity`, `meal`, `rest`); `start_time`; `duration_min`; `end_time` (derived); `origin` (`model`, `fallback_rule_based`, `user`); `is_locked`; `must_visit` (derived, `trip_places`); `note` (**ai_written** when `note_origin = ai`), `note_origin` (`ai`, `user`, `none`); `cost` `{min, max, currency, label}` or null (`cost_*`); `travel_from_previous` `{minutes, distance_m, mode, source}` or null (`travel_from_prev_min`, `travel_from_prev_m`, `travel_mode`, `travel_source`) |
| Finding | `id`; `code` (13 codes, §8); `severity` (`error`, `warning`, `info`); `message`; `day_number`; `item_id`; `place_id` (set only for `MUST_VISIT_MISSING`, whose `item_id` is null, IMD-42); `suggested_fix` |
| Totals | `currency`; `estimate` `{min, max}`; `planning_total`; `complete` (bool); `incomplete_count` |
| EditResultOut | `plan_revision`; `changed_days[]` (full Day objects); `totals`; `findings[]` (all findings of the new revision) |

Fields marked **ai_written** carry model text and nothing else; the web app renders them with AiBadge (FR-035). No other response field contains model-written text: names, prices, hours, times, travel and totals always come from the database or the backend calculation. In the extension, the day `explanation` is **ai_written**; the proposals of `TripIntakeOut` and the packing items with `origin ai` are model suggestions that passed code checks, and are shown as "AI-suggested" until the traveller confirms or accepts them.

**CostSummaryOut** (computed by `budget/engine.py`, §9; nothing stored except `budget_settings`)

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| currency | Trip currency (budget currency, else destination currency) |
| estimate | `{min, max}` = BF-07 (items plus traveller inputs) |
| contingency | `{pct, amount}` = BF-08; `pct` from `budget_settings.contingency_pct` (0 when the contingency feature is disabled) |
| planning_total | BF-09 |
| per_traveller | `{travellers, largest_share, label: "average"}` = BF-10 |
| budget | `{amount, status: none \| near \| exceeded, ratio_pct, excess}` = BF-11 (`excess` null unless exceeded) |
| by_day[] | `{day_number, min, max, contingency_share}`; sums equal `planning_total` (FR-073 AC1) |
| by_category[] | `{category: activities \| food \| transport \| accommodation \| other \| contingency, min, max, label}`; transport and accommodation lines carry `label: "traveller_input"` or `"unavailable"` (FR-072) |
| alerts[] | `BUDGET_NEAR`, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` findings (empty when the budget-alerts feature is disabled) |
| complete, incomplete_items[] | `COST_INCOMPLETE` status and the item IDs left out (FR-071 AC2) |
| settings | `{transport_allowance_per_day, stay_budget_per_night, contingency_pct}` (`budget_settings`) |

**VersionOut** (`itinerary_versions`): `id`, `version_no`, `name` (null for automatic snapshots), `reason` (`generation`, `regeneration`, `edit`, `restore`, `fallback`, `manual`); `kind` derived: `named` when `name` is set, else `automatic`, `plan_revision`, `validation_summary`, `generation_id`, `created_at`. The `snapshot` is stored in format `snap-1` (days and items without costs or findings, §5.2) and never returned raw; API-24 with `version_id` builds an `ItineraryOut` from it on read by running the budget engine and the validator, without writing anything (IMD-18).

**Profile** (`profiles`): `id`, `email` (from the token, not stored), `display_name` (1 to 60), `home_country`, `preferred_currency`, `default_preferences` (PreferencesIn without `notes` and `must_visit_place_ids`), `ai_notice_ack_at`. In `ProfilePatch` the flag `ai_notice_acknowledged: true` sets `ai_notice_ack_at = now()`.

**Destination**: `id`, `slug`, `name`, `region`, `country_code`, `timezone`, `currency`, `is_sample` (true for the SAMPLE fixture destination; the web shows a SAMPLE banner), `center` `{lat, lon}`, `bbox`.

### 6.5.1 Extension schemas (EXT)

The schemas below belong to the extension endpoints of §6.6.7 (release EXT, Sprints 5 to 7, each behind its switch). Scores and weights are JSON numbers with four decimals; temperatures and precipitation are numbers with one decimal; money follows IMD-05.

**Day (extension fields)**: when `day_explain` is enabled, each `Day` of `ItineraryOut` and `EditResultOut` also carries `explanation` (**ai_written**, ≤ 400 characters, or null), `explanation_origin` (`ai` or `none`), `explanation_current` (bool, derived: `explanation_revision = trips.plan_revision`) and `explanation_generated_at` (ts or null). The web app shows an out-of-date explanation greyed with "Refresh" and never as current (FR-129 AC3).

**WhyOut** (API-63; computed by `generation/ranking.py` `explain_components()`, nothing stored)

| Field | Type | Rule | DB source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trip_id, place_id | uuid | place active and of the trip's destination, else 404 | path |
| mapping_version | str | preference mapping version (`pm-1`, IMD-29) | code constant |
| included | bool | false when a hard filter removes the place | derived |
| hard_filter | enum or null | `step_free_required`, `excluded_category`, `closed_on_all_trip_days`, `over_activity_budget`; set only when `included` is false | derived (§8.9 hard filters) |
| must_visit | bool | a must-visit place is never filtered (FR-027 AC2) | `trip_places` |
| score | number or null | null when `included` is false; equals the candidate-ranking score for the same inputs (TC-399) | derived |
| components[] | object[] | `{name: interest \| price \| distance \| pace \| signal, weight, value (0 to 1) or null, contribution, status: ok \| unavailable \| not_used, text}`; `unavailable` uses the formula's neutral value (price 0.5) and says so; `signal` is `not_used` in the MVP (weight 0) | derived |
| summary | str | one sentence built from a code template (for example "Ranked high for your interests museums and history; price unavailable"), never model text | derived |

**TripIntakeIn / TripIntakeOut** (API-64; `trips/schemas.py`; nothing stored except the assist-call row)

| Field | Type | In | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| text | str | yes | 1 to 1,000 characters after trimming; control characters removed; sent to the model only as quoted data, with e-mail addresses and phone numbers replaced by `[redacted]` (as `notes`, §8.6) |
| status | enum | – | `ok`; `unavailable` when the provider failed or every value was rejected (the screen then offers the manual form) |
| resolved_relative_to | date | – | today's date in the proposed destination's time zone (UTC when no destination was found); relative dates such as "next weekend" are resolved against it |
| trip | object | – | a TripIn with every field optional: only values that pass the TripIn validators (§6.5) are present; `destination_id` only for an active supported destination |
| preferences | object | – | a PreferencesIn with every field optional, under the same rule; `must_visit_place_ids` only for active places of the proposed destination |
| unresolved[] | object[] | – | `{field or null, text, reason: not_understood \| unsupported_destination \| invalid_value}`; `text` is the fragment of the traveller's own words, never model prose |
| origin | enum | – | always `ai_suggested`: the web marks every pre-filled field "suggested, check before saving" until confirmed (FR-128 AC1) |

**DayExplanationOut** (API-65): `day_number`; `status` (`ok`, `unavailable`); `explanation` (**ai_written**, null when unavailable); `explanation_origin`; `plan_revision` (the revision it explains); `explanation_current`; `explanation_generated_at`.

**OptimisePreviewOut / OptimiseApplyIn** (API-66, API-67; `itinerary/optimise.py`, pure)

| Field | Type | In | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| day_number, plan_revision | int | apply: `plan_revision` | the preview names the revision it was computed on |
| status | enum | – | `proposal`; `no_better_order` (saving under 5 minutes); `nothing_to_optimise` (fewer than three movable items) |
| current_order, proposed_order | uuid[] | apply: `item_ids` (the proposed order) | item IDs of the whole day; locked items and meal slots keep their positions |
| fixed_item_ids | uuid[] | – | locked items and meal slots |
| travel_minutes_before, travel_minutes_after, saving_min | int | – | sums of `travel_from_previous.minutes` over the day; `saving_min` ≥ 5 when `status = proposal` |
| estimated | bool | – | true when any pair used the fallback distance estimate (§9) |
| findings_after[] | Finding[] | – | validator result for the proposed day; a proposal that would add an error finding is never returned |

**ForecastOut** (API-68; `weather/service.py`)

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| trip_id, status | `ok`; `partial` (some days outside the 16-day window); `none_in_window` (no trip day within 16 days); `unavailable` (Open-Meteo failed or timed out after `WEATHER_TIMEOUT_S`, NFR-006) |
| source | `{name: "Open-Meteo", licence: "CC BY 4.0", attribution_text, url}`, shown next to the forecast (EXT_CONTRACT §8) |
| fetched_at | ts of the cached rows (`weather_cache.fetched_at`) or null |
| days[] | `{day_number, date, in_window, precip_probability_max (0 to 100 or null), precipitation_sum_mm, weather_code, temp_max_c, temp_min_c, outdoor_share_pct, rain_flag}`; `rain_flag` = `in_window` and `precip_probability_max` ≥ 60 and `outdoor_share_pct` ≥ 50 (items whose place has `indoor = false`, by duration) |
| suggestion | `{day_a, day_b, reason}` or null: at most one; `day_b` is the trip day in the window with the lowest `precip_probability_max`, which must be below 60 (ties: the earlier day); never suggested when either day has a locked item or when the validator would report a new error after the swap |

**SwapDaysIn** (API-69): `{plan_revision, day_a, day_b}`; different, else 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`; a day number outside the plan gives 422 `INVALID_EDIT` (as API-69). Response `EditResultOut` with both days in `changed_days`.

**TodayOut** (API-70; `itinerary/today.py`, pure)

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| trip_id, date, time | the query values, or today's date and time in the destination time zone when omitted |
| status | `before_first_stop`, `at_stop`, `between_stops`, `day_finished`, `not_a_trip_day`, `no_itinerary` |
| day_number | int or null |
| current | `{item_id, place_name, start_time, end_time}` or null |
| next | `{item_id, place_name, start_time, planned_departure, travel_minutes, travel_source}` or null; `planned_departure` = next `start_time` − `travel_minutes` |
| plan_revision | int or null |

**BudgetFitOut** (API-71; `budget/fit.py`, pure, over the budget engine)

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| currency, budget, planning_total | money (IMD-05); `budget` null when the trip has none |
| status | `within_budget` (no suggestions), `suggestions`, `no_fit` (no change of at most two items within the 12 costliest removable items reaches the budget), `no_budget` |
| suggestions[] | at most 3: `{id, changes: [{action: remove \| replace, item_id, day_number, place: {id, name}, replacement: PlaceSummary or null}], saving, new_planning_total, lost}`; `saving` and `new_planning_total` are money computed by the budget engine; `lost` is a code-built sentence ("Loses Fort Museum, 90 min, day 2"); must-visit and locked items never appear; a `replace` uses only a current alternative of API-28 |
| apply | the client applies a change with API-27 (remove) or API-29 (replace) and the current `plan_revision`; a two-change suggestion is applied as two edits, the second with the revision returned by the first |

**ContextCardOut** (API-72, API-73; `context_cards`): `subject_type`, `subject_id`, `source` (`wikivoyage`, `wikipedia`), `page_title`, `extract` (≤ 1,200 characters, plain text), `page_url`, `licence` (`CC BY-SA 4.0`), `attribution_text` ("Text from Wikivoyage, CC BY-SA 4.0"), `retrieved_at`, `expires_at`. API-73 returns the Wikivoyage card when one exists, otherwise the Wikipedia card. Extracts are descriptive only: prices, hours and availability always come from `places` (PR-01).

**PackingListOut / PackingItem / PackingRefineIn / PackingItemPatch** (API-43, API-74, API-75; `prep/schemas.py`, `checklist_items`)

| Schema | Fields and rules |
| --- | --- |
| PackingItem | `id`, `label`, `category`, `origin` (`rule`, `ai`, `user`), `status` (`active`, `suggested`, `rejected`), `is_checked`, `sort_order`; `origin ai` is shown with the label "AI-suggested" (NFR-040) |
| PackingListOut | `trip_id`; `rules_version` (`pk-1`); `items[]` (`rejected` items are left out); `counts` `{total, checked, suggested}` |
| PackingRefineIn | `{need}`: 1 to 200 characters after trimming; control characters removed; sent to the model only as quoted data |
| PackingRefineOut | `{status: ok \| unavailable, added: PackingItem[], dropped_count, list: PackingListOut}`; `dropped_count` counts off-vocabulary, duplicate and over-limit items |
| PackingItemPatch | any of `is_checked` (only for `status active`, else 422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`), `status` (`active` to accept or `rejected` to reject, only from `suggested`), `label` (1 to 160 characters, only for `status active`; the item becomes `origin user`) |

### 6.6.5 Itinerary, edits and versions (MOD-B08, MOD-B07)

API-30 and API-31 are handled in `app/generation/router.py` (MOD-B06) because they start generation jobs; the itinerary service still writes the plan (IMD-13). Edits, replacements, version saves and restores (API-25 to API-29, API-37, API-38) are refused with 409 `GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` while a generation for the trip is active (IMD-23).

All edit endpoints (API-25 to API-29) run one transaction: lock the trip row (`select … for update`), compare `plan_revision`, apply the operation, recalculate times and travel for the changed days (routing, §9), recalculate costs (budget engine), revalidate the whole plan, replace the warnings, increment `plan_revision`, write an automatic version (`reason edit`, IMD-18), commit, and return 200 `EditResultOut` (FR-064). Soft-rule breaks are accepted and reported as findings (PR-06); structural errors return 422 `INVALID_EDIT`. Tests for all of them: `tests/api/test_edits.py` plus the cases listed.

### 6.6.7 Extension endpoints (EXT: MOD-B03, MOD-B06, MOD-B08, MOD-B09, MOD-B12, MOD-B16, MOD-B17)

These 14 endpoints (API-43 and API-63 to API-75) belong to the extension release, built in Sprints 5 to 7 after the MVP core. Each sits behind one switch of `FEATURES_DISABLED` (the "Switch" row): while its switch is listed, the route returns 404 `NOT_FOUND` exactly like an unknown route and the web app hides its entry point (IMD-11, TC-432). The common rules are:

- Authorization follows §6.2: API-72 and API-73 are reference data; all others are owned routes and are in the two-user suite `tests/authz/test_ownership.py` (TC-431).
- The three assist endpoints (API-64, API-65, API-74) call the active provider through one ModelProvider operation each (§8): `extract_trip_request` (schema `ti-1`), `explain_day` (`de-1`) and `suggest_packing_items` (`ps-1`).
- Before any of those calls, the server checks `profiles.ai_notice_ack_at` (else 422, field `ai_notice`). It also checks the daily assist cap: the caller's `ai_assist_calls` rows since 00:00 UTC must number fewer than `AI_DAILY_ASSIST_CALLS_PER_USER` (Proposed 30), else 429 `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` with `details` `[{field: "scope", message: "assist"}]`. Assist calls do not count against the generation caps, and generations do not count against the assist cap.
- Every assist call writes exactly one `ai_assist_calls` row (status `ok`, `rejected` or `failed`; no prompt or output text, NFR-024).
- A provider failure or a rejected output is never an HTTP error: the endpoint returns 200 with `status unavailable` and stores nothing else.
- API-67 and API-69 are edits: they follow the edit transaction of §6.6.5 and §5.8 exactly (409 `STALE_PLAN`, 409 `GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS`, 409 `CONFLICT` on an archived trip, version `reason edit`, 200 `EditResultOut`).
- Rate limiting (§6.1) also applies to API-64, API-65, API-67, API-69 and API-74.

| Endpoints | Release | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API-05 delete account | R2 | FR-006; deletion on request is an operator procedure in the MVP (NFR-022) |
| API-18 nearby places | T1 | FR-021 |
| API-39 to API-41 share link and shared view | T1 | FR-098 |
| API-42 place feedback | T1 | FR-111, FR-112 |
| API-44 to API-48 clothing, booking tasks, readiness | T1 / R2 | FR-090, FR-091, FR-107 to FR-110 (API-43 packing moved to the extension release, §6.6.7) |

| API-59, API-60 assistant proposals | R2 | FR-070 |

None of these routes, nor their tables, exists in the MVP or extension code; they stay unbuilt in this project, and a T1 route is added only after its task card is written and SG-7 allows it. The extension routes of §6.6.7 exist in the code but return 404 `NOT_FOUND` while their switch is listed in `FEATURES_DISABLED`; an extension that is never started has no route at all. In-app flight and hotel booking is not part of any release (EXT_CONTRACT; PR-10: external booking links are enough). Routes that never exist: provider, model or prompt selection over HTTP, evaluation runs, administrative or cross-user routes, raw query or export routes, routes that accept a user ID (blueprint §17.8).

# 7. Frontend implementation specification

This section fixes what `apps/web` must build: rules for every screen, the 14 MVP routes, the shared components and the mapping from page to component to endpoint. Field names come from the API contract (§6); the database is never reached from the browser. Background and rationale: blueprint §10, §12 and §15.9.

## 7.1 Architecture rules

| Concern | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Rendering | Route files under `app/(public)` and `app/(app)` are thin server components that render one client page component. All data for signed-in pages is fetched in the browser with TanStack Query, because the access token lives in the browser session. No server component calls FastAPI with a user token in the MVP (Provisional) |
| API client | `lib/api/client.ts` wraps openapi-fetch over the generated `lib/api/schema.d.ts` (IMD-06). Base URL `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`. Every call adds `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` from the Supabase session and an `X-Request-ID` UUID |
| 401 handling | On 401 the client calls `supabase.auth.refreshSession()` once and repeats the request once. A second 401 signs out locally and redirects to `/sign-in?next=<current path>` |
| Error mapping | Every non-2xx response is parsed as the error envelope (§6) into an `ApiError {status, code, message, details, requestId, retryAfterS}`. A table in `lib/api/errors.ts` maps `code` to UI behaviour: `VALIDATION_ERROR` and `INVALID_EDIT` → field or inline messages from `details`; `NOT_FOUND` → not-found screen; `STALE_PLAN` → reload the itinerary and show a toast; `GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS` → show the running job and keep edit controls disabled until it ends (IMD-23); `CONFLICT` → message from the envelope (for example an archived, read-only trip, IMD-35); `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` → "Not available yet" (temporary, IMD-37); `RATE_LIMITED` and `AI_QUOTA_REACHED` → message with `retry_after_s` or the reset time; `INTERNAL` and `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` → ErrorState with the request ID. A network failure (no response) shows an offline banner and keeps form input |
| Query hooks | All hooks and query keys live in `lib/api/queries.ts` (§7.4). Components never call `fetch` directly |
| No fabrication | The web app never computes or invents itinerary content, times, durations, travel times, prices, totals, budget status, labels or success states. It renders what the API returned. While a mutation is in flight it shows a saving state and changes no number. It shows "Saved" only after a 2xx response |
| Money and time | Amounts arrive as decimal strings with a `currency` (IMD-05). `lib/format/money.ts` formats them with `Intl.NumberFormat` and never adds them. Dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and times (`HH:MM`, destination time zone) are displayed as received, never shifted to the browser time zone |
| Secrets | Only the `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables of §H of the contract may be read in `apps/web`. No Gemini, routing, database or service-role key exists in the web code or bundle; the CI build check of IMP-102 fails if one appears |
| Feature switches | `lib/flags.ts` reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURES_DISABLED` (IMD-11). A disabled cut-list feature hides its controls and its route renders the not-found screen |
| Code loading | MapLibre and dnd-kit are imported only by the itinerary page (dynamic import), so other pages stay light |

## 7.2 Authentication state and AuthGuard

| Item | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Client | `lib/auth/supabase.ts` creates one browser client with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` |
| Session hook | `lib/auth/useSession.ts` exposes `{status: loading or signed_in or signed_out, user, accessToken}` and subscribes to `onAuthStateChange` |
| AuthGuard | `components/shell/AuthGuard.tsx`, used by `app/(app)/layout.tsx`. While `loading` it shows LoadingSkeleton; when `signed_out` it redirects to `/sign-in?next=<path>`; when `signed_in` it renders children and loads `['me']` (API-03) once |
| Sign-up and sign-in | Direct calls to Supabase Auth from the browser; the backend never receives a password (FR-001, FR-002). `auth/callback/route.ts` exchanges the confirmation code for a session and redirects to `next` or `/dashboard` |
| Sign-out | `supabase.auth.signOut()`, then `queryClient.clear()`, then redirect to `/sign-in` |
| Public routes | `/`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up`, `/auth/callback`. A signed-in user who opens `/sign-in` is sent to `/dashboard` |

## 7.3 Forms and validation

Each form uses react-hook-form with a zod schema in `lib/validation/`. The schemas mirror the server rules of §6. The server remains the authority: a 422 response maps `details[].field` onto the form fields and keeps all input.

| Form (schema file) | Field rules |
| --- | --- |
| Sign-up (`auth.ts`) | email: valid format; password: at least 8 characters. Message for an existing account is non-revealing: "Try signing in instead" (FR-001 AC2) |
| Sign-in (`auth.ts`) | email format; password required. Error text does not say which field was wrong |
| Trip details (`trip.ts`) | title 1 to 120 characters; destination_id from the API-06 list; start_date and end_date required, end on or after start, 1 to 14 days; adults 1 to 20, children 0 to 20; budget amount greater than 0 with a currency from the supported list, both set or both empty; the budget is labelled "total for the whole group" |
| Budget settings (`budget.ts`) | nightly stay budget 0 or more; daily transport allowance 0 or more; contingency percentage 0 to 50, default 10 (database check of `budget_settings.contingency_pct`; §6 is authoritative) |
| Preferences (`preferences.ts`) | interests from the category list; pace in relaxed, balanced, busy; budget_priority, transport_pref, accommodation_type from fixed lists of §6; step_free_required boolean; notes up to 1,000 characters with the hint "Do not enter personal details"; must_visit_place_ids only picked from places of the trip's destination |
| Item edit (`edit.ts`) | duration whole minutes 15 to 480; start time `HH:MM`; day number 1 to the trip's day count. A start time outside the day window is allowed and produces a warning from the server, not a client error |
| Version name (`version.ts`) | 1 to 60 characters (IMD-18; the database allows 80); a duplicate name comes back as 409 `CONFLICT` and is shown on the field |
| Profile (`profile.ts`) | display_name 1 to 60 characters (FR-004 AC1); preferred_currency from the supported list |

## 7.4 Shared state, query keys and invalidation

TanStack Query is the only cache. Server data is never copied into global stores. UI-only state (open dialogs, selected day tab, filter inputs) lives in the page or in the URL query string (filters, selected day), so reload and back keep it.

| Query key | Endpoint | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `['me']` | API-03 | AuthGuard, profile |
| `['destinations']` | API-06 | Wizard, explore |
| `['trips', filters]` | API-08 | Dashboard |
| `['latestItinerary']` | API-09 | Dashboard shortcut |
| `['trip', tripId]` | API-10 | All trip pages (header, stale banner) |
| `['preferences', tripId]` | API-15 | Wizard |
| `['places', destinationId, filters]` | API-16 | Explore, add-place dialog |
| `['place', placeId]` | API-17 | PlaceDetailDrawer |
| `['savedPlaces', tripId]` | API-21 | Explore |
| `['generation', generationId]` | API-23 | Generate page (polling) |
| `['itinerary', tripId, versionId or 'current']` | API-24 | Itinerary page |
| `['alternatives', itemId]` | API-28 | AlternativesDialog |
| `['costs', tripId]` | API-33 | Costs page, cost strip |
| `['summary', tripId]` | API-35 | Summary page |
| `['versions', tripId]` | API-36 | Versions page |
| `['why', tripId, placeId]` | API-63 (EXT) | WhyThisPlacePanel |
| `['weather', tripId]` | API-68 (EXT) | ForecastBanner |
| `['today', tripId, date]` | API-70 (EXT) | TodayView |
| `['budgetFit', tripId]` | API-71 (EXT) | BudgetFitPanel |
| `['context', 'place' or 'destination', id]` | API-72, API-73 (EXT) | ContextCard |
| `['packing', tripId]` | API-43 (EXT) | PackingList |

| Mutation | Endpoint | On success |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create trip | API-07 | invalidate `trips`; navigate to the next wizard step |
| Update trip (settings, rename, archive) | API-11 | set `trip` from the response; invalidate `trips`, `itinerary`, `costs`, `summary` (plan may now be stale) |
| Delete, duplicate trip | API-12, API-13 | invalidate `trips`, `latestItinerary` |
| Save preferences | API-14 | invalidate `preferences`, `trip` |
| Save or unsave place | API-19, API-20 | invalidate `savedPlaces` |
| Start generation, regenerate day or plan | API-22, API-30, API-31 | store the generation id; poll `generation`. On `completed`: invalidate `trip`, `itinerary`, `costs`, `summary`, `versions`, `trips`, `latestItinerary` |
| Edit item (add, move, retime, lock, remove, replace) | API-25 to API-27, API-29 | write the returned `plan_revision`, changed days, totals and findings into `itinerary`; invalidate `costs`, `summary`, `versions`. On 409 `STALE_PLAN`: invalidate `itinerary` and show "This plan changed since you opened it" |
| Re-validate | API-32 | replace findings in `itinerary` |
| Budget settings | API-34 | invalidate `costs`, `itinerary` (budget findings change) |
| Save or restore version | API-37, API-38 | invalidate `versions`; restore also invalidates `itinerary`, `costs`, `summary`, `trip` |
| Update profile | API-04 | set `me` |
| Describe trip (EXT) | API-64 | show the proposal in IntakeConfirmation; nothing cached; confirmed fields go through "Create trip" and "Save preferences" |
| Explain day (EXT) | API-65 | write the explanation into `itinerary` for that day |
| Optimise preview / apply (EXT) | API-66 / API-67 | preview held in the dialog; apply as "Edit item" (revision, `STALE_PLAN` handling) and invalidate `weather`, `today`, `budgetFit` |
| Swap days (EXT) | API-69 | as "Edit item"; invalidate `weather`, `today` |
| Apply budget-fit suggestion (EXT) | API-27 or API-29 | as "Edit item"; invalidate `budgetFit` |
| Refine or update packing (EXT) | API-74, API-75 | set `packing` from the response |

Generation polling: first poll 2 s after the 202, then 3, 4 and 5 s, then every 5 s; stop on `completed` or `failed`. If the status is still not terminal 160 s after the start, stop polling and offer "Reload status" (IMD-12). Polling pauses while the tab is hidden and resumes on focus.

| Data on screen | Source field | Shown as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price or hours with label `curated` | `price_label`, `hours_label`, `hours_checked_on` | "Curated, checked on <date>" |
| Price or hours with label `estimate` | same | "Estimate" |
| Price or hours with label `unavailable` | same | "Unavailable" (never a guessed value) |
| Travel time from the routing service | `travel_source = routing_api` | "Estimated travel time from a routing service" |
| Travel time from the distance fallback | `travel_source = fallback_estimate` | "Estimated travel time (distance based)" |
| Day theme, item note, summary text written by the model | fields marked AI-written in §6 | AiBadge "AI-written" |
| Plan from the rule-based planner | `outcome = fallback_rule_based` | FallbackNotice "Built by rules because the AI service was unavailable or its answer failed checks" |
| Fixture data or saved sample plan | destination flag or plan source in §6 | SampleBanner "SAMPLE data, not a real destination" |
| Day explanation (EXT) | de-1 output | AiBadge "AI-written" |
| Intake proposal, AI packing suggestion (EXT) | ti-1, ps-1 output (passed code checks) | "AI-suggested" until the traveller confirms or accepts (§6.5); intake values marked "Check before saving" |
| Ranking explanation (EXT) | API-63 components | "Why this place was ranked here" (computed by rules, no AiBadge) |
| Forecast (EXT) | API-68 `source`, `attribution` | "Forecast: <probability>% chance of rain" with "Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0)"; never shown as certain |
| Context card (EXT) | `source`, `licence`, `page_url` | "From Wikivoyage" or "From Wikipedia", "CC BY-SA 4.0" and a link to the page; no prices or hours taken from it |
| Booking (excluded) | none | Nothing: no screen offers or implies booking (§1.3 and IMD-46) |

Rules: no screen says or implies that a price, opening time or route is live or verified (FR-076, FR-117); no screen says or implies that the AI is accurate; totals always carry "Estimate" and the completeness note when `complete` is false; a fallback plan is never presented as an AI result; EXT screens show amounts, savings and travel minutes only as returned by the server (no browser arithmetic).
