### IMP-407 Edit transaction core: recalculate and revalidate every edit atomically with plan revision

| Task | Sprint 4 (week 4) · CODE · 5 points · lead Het · release MVP |
| --- | --- |
| Objective | Every itinerary edit runs through one edit pipeline that, in a single transaction, checks plan_revision, applies the operation, recalculates times and costs, revalidates, saves warnings, increments plan_revision and returns the recalculated day, totals and findings. |
| Owners and parts | Het — whole task (5 points); branch `feat/IMP-407-<short>` |
| Traces to | Stories US-073; FR-064; NFR-003, NFR-008 |
| Dependencies | Prerequisites: IMP-308, IMP-404 · Downstream: IMP-408, IMP-409, IMP-499, IMP-504, IMP-505, IMP-506, IMP-610, IMP-612, IMP-710 |
| Files | apps/api/app/itinerary/edits.py (create); apps/api/app/itinerary/service.py (modify); apps/api/app/itinerary/schemas.py (modify); apps/api/tests/api/test_edits.py (create); apps/api/tests/api/test_edit_performance.py (create) |
| Implementation | 1. Define EditOperation variants (move, retime, remove, add, lock, replace) and apply_edit(trip_id, user_id, base_revision, op) in app/itinerary/edits.py; locking the trip row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) inside the transaction.<br>2. If base_revision != trips.plan_revision raise StalePlan -> 409 STALE_PLAN with nothing changed (full UX in IMP-504).<br>3. Before the revision check refuse with 409 GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS when a generation for the trip is queued, running, validating or repairing (IMD-23).<br>4. Structurally impossible edits (day out of range, unknown place, moving a locked item) raise InvalidEdit -> 422 INVALID_EDIT.<br>5. After applying: schedule.recalculate (IMP-308), budget engine, validator (IMP-404); save items, warnings for the new revision, plan_revision + 1, and an automatic itinerary_versions row with reason edit (IMD-18; pruned by IMP-610; with the versions switch off only one backup copy is kept).<br>6. Edits with resulting conflicts succeed and return the findings (PR-06); only impossible edits are rejected.<br>7. Edit response schema: {plan_revision, day (recalculated), totals, warnings}; the web replaces its cache with it. |
| Interfaces | API: API-25, API-26, API-27, API-29 · Tables: itinerary_items, itinerary_warnings, itinerary_versions, trips · Modules: MOD-B08, MOD-B07, MOD-B09 |
| Acceptance criteria | - FR-064 AC1-AC2 hold (TC-206, TC-207): every edit response has recalculated totals; a failing validation step leaves data consistent and is reported.<br>- An interrupted edit leaves consistent data (TC-312, fault injection).<br>- Edit recalculation on a 10-day fixture stays under the p95 1.5 s target locally (TC-330, recorded, not a gate).<br>- A stale base revision returns 409 STALE_PLAN and changes nothing.<br>- An edit while a generation for the trip is active returns 409 GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS and changes nothing (IMD-23). |
| Tests | apps/api/tests/api/test_edits.py — TC-206, TC-207, TC-312 — `make test-api ARGS='-k edits'`<br>apps/api/tests/api/test_edit_performance.py — TC-330 — `make test-api ARGS='-k edit_performance'` |
| Completion evidence | PR with make check green.; Timing output of the 10-day fixture test in the PR. |

| Task | Sprint 5 (week 5) · CODE · 5 points · lead Junaid with Manal · release MVP |
| --- | --- |
| Objective | The validator emits CLOSED_ON_DAY, OUTSIDE_HOURS, HOURS_UNVERIFIED, DAY_TOO_LONG, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, BUDGET_NEAR, COST_INCOMPLETE and ESTIMATE_USED with the §8/§9 severities after every generation, edit and API-32 call. |
| Owners and parts | Junaid (lead) — Opening-hours and overpacked-day checks (3 points)<br>Manal — Budget conflict check (2 points)<br>One branch and pull request per part (`feat/IMP-501-<part>`); the backend, database or AI part merges first |
| Traces to | Stories US-062, US-063; FR-052 to FR-054; NFR-003, NFR-030, NFR-040 |
| Dependencies | Prerequisites: IMP-404, IMP-308 · Downstream: IMP-599, IMP-608, IMP-710 |
| Files | apps/api/app/validation/rules.py (modify); apps/api/app/validation/validator.py (modify); apps/api/app/generation/pipeline.py (modify); apps/api/tests/unit/validation/test_hours.py (create); apps/api/tests/unit/validation/test_day_length_budget.py (create); apps/api/tests/api/test_itinerary.py (modify) |
| Implementation | 1. Add the opening-hours rule to rules.py following the six-row decision list of §9 (blueprint §20.4): unavailable label or no rows -> HOURS_UNVERIFIED (info, no conflict claimed); previous-weekday row closing after midnight that covers the visit -> no finding; no row for the weekday -> HOURS_UNVERIFIED; closed row -> CLOSED_ON_DAY (error); visit inside an open row -> none; otherwise OUTSIDE_HOURS (error).<br>2. Evaluate start and end in the destination's local time zone (destinations.timezone) from itinerary_days.plan_date + start_time; never in UTC.<br>3. Add DAY_TOO_LONG (warning): active minutes = sum(duration_min) + sum(travel_from_prev_min) per day; compare with the pace preset of trip_preferences.pace (relaxed 3 items/300 min, balanced 5/480, busy 7/600, from settings, Provisional) and include both figures in the message.<br>4. Add the budget rules by calling the pure budget engine (app/budget/engine.py, BF-11) instead of re-computing totals: BUDGET_EXCEEDED (warning, message carries the excess as a money string) if P > B; BUDGET_NEAR (info) if 100*P >= theta*B with theta = 90 (code constant BUDGET_NEAR_PCT in app/budget/engine.py, IMD-29); no finding when the budget is empty or zero.<br>5. Add COST_INCOMPLETE (warning, trip-level) when any item cost_label is unavailable or uses a category estimate, and ESTIMATE_USED (info, item-level) for each item priced by a category estimate (BF-04).<br>6. Register the new rules in validator.py so pipeline step 9, the edit pipeline (IMP-407) and API-32 all run the same rule list; findings are persisted to itinerary_warnings by the existing writer (IMP-405).<br>7. Write boundary unit tests: closed day, unknown hours, overnight row, local time zone, pace limits at exactly the limit and one above, budget at 89, 90 and 101 percent. |
| Interfaces | API: API-32, API-24 · Tables: itinerary_warnings, place_opening_hours, trip_preferences, destinations · Modules: MOD-B07, MOD-B09 · Other: finding codes §8, BF-11, constant BUDGET_NEAR_PCT in app/budget/engine.py (IMD-29) |
| Acceptance criteria | - FR-052 AC1-AC2, FR-053 AC1-AC2 and FR-054 AC1-AC2 hold (TC-180 to TC-185).<br>- A visit crossing midnight on an overnight row produces no finding (TC-301); hours are compared in destination local time (TC-302).<br>- Pace and near-budget thresholds are exact at the boundary (TC-303, TC-304).<br>- A place with unavailable hours never produces CLOSED_ON_DAY or OUTSIDE_HOURS.<br>- Budget findings are never repaired by dropping items (checked by a unit test on repair input). |

### IMP-502 Bounded repair with at most one model retry

| Task | Sprint 5 (week 5) · CODE · 5 points · lead Nidhi · release MVP-S |
| --- | --- |
| Objective | Invalid plans are repaired deterministically first, then by at most one model call with the whole request and the exact findings, and anything unresolved is saved as visible findings or replaced by the rule-based plan. |
| Owners and parts | Nidhi — whole task (5 points); branch `feat/IMP-502-<short>` |
| Traces to | Stories US-066; FR-057; NFR-007, NFR-030 |
| Dependencies | Prerequisites: IMP-405, IMP-403 · Downstream: IMP-599, IMP-607 |
| Files | apps/api/app/validation/repair.py (create); apps/api/app/generation/pipeline.py (modify); apps/api/tests/unit/validation/test_repair.py (create); apps/api/tests/api/test_generations.py (modify); apps/api/app/ai/prompts/templates/itinerary_generate/v1/repair.txt (create) |
| Implementation | 1. Implement deterministic repair in repair.py (pure, no I/O): forward-shift start times to max(own start, previous end + travel + buffer) skipping locked items; then for error findings in the fixed order UNKNOWN_PLACE, OUTSIDE_TRIP_DATES, CLOSED_ON_DAY, OUTSIDE_HOURS, OVERLAP apply the cheapest fix (move to another day with room, swap with next item, drop the lowest-ranked unlocked non-must-visit item); insert a missing must-visit into the best day with room; count each fix.<br>2. Never change prices, hours or travel times; never move is_locked items; never drop must-visit places; never act on budget findings.<br>3. In pipeline step 10 (pipeline.py): after deterministic repair, revalidate; if errors remain and repair_attempts = 0, make exactly one provider call with the previous output and the exact findings in repair_context using the itinerary_generate/v1 template with its repair.txt appended (§8.5, §8.13), with its own 25 s allowance and no transport retry; set ai_generations.repair_attempts = 1 and status repairing.<br>4. Revalidate the repaired output; if usable (at least one item and none of UNKNOWN_PLACE, OUTSIDE_TRIP_DATES, OVERLAP, CLOSED_ON_DAY remains, §8.12) save with outcome model_repaired and the remaining warnings; otherwise build the rule-based plan (IMP-402) and save with outcome fallback_rule_based, failure_reason null and validation_summary.provider_failure = unresolved_validation (returned as fallback_reason, IMD-22).<br>5. Store deterministic_repairs count and the validation_summary on ai_generations.<br>6. Add tests with the MOCK scenarios invalid_json and unknown_place and flawed (overlap and missing must-visit place); assert the provider call count via the mock call log. |
| Interfaces | API: API-22, API-23 · Tables: ai_generations, itinerary_warnings · Modules: MOD-B07, MOD-B06, MOD-B05 · Env: MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO · Other: repair_context (§8), prompt template itinerary_repair v1 |
| Acceptance criteria | - FR-057 AC1-AC3 hold (TC-190 to TC-192).<br>- Invalid model output is routed to repair, never to a blind retry (TC-011); the mock records at most 2 calls per generation (1 generate + 1 repair).<br>- Locked items and must-visit places are unchanged by repair (TC-313 repair part).<br>- Repair terminates on every fixture (no loop) and repair_attempts is never above 1 (DB check constraint). |
| Tests | apps/api/tests/unit/validation/test_repair.py — TC-190, TC-313 — `make test-unit ARGS='-k repair'`<br>apps/api/tests/api/test_generations.py — TC-011, TC-191, TC-192 — `make test-api ARGS='-k repair'` |
| Completion evidence | PR with make check green; Test log showing provider call counts per scenario; API-23 JSON of a model_repaired generation from the MOCK scenario |

| Task | Sprint 5 (week 5) · CODE · 5 points · lead Kirtan · release MVP |
| --- | --- |
| Objective | Expensive endpoints are rate limited per user and per address with 429 RATE_LIMITED, and generation is refused with 429 AI_QUOTA_REACHED before any provider call when the per-user or global daily cap is reached. |

| Traces to | Stories US-009, US-040; FR-046, FR-126; NFR-017, NFR-037, NFR-039 |
| Dependencies | Prerequisites: IMP-202, IMP-201 · Downstream: IMP-599, IMP-702 |
| Files | apps/api/app/core/rate_limit.py (modify); apps/api/app/generation/service.py (modify); apps/api/app/ai/limits.py (modify); apps/api/app/ai/providers/gemini.py (modify); apps/api/tests/api/test_generations.py (modify); apps/api/tests/unit/core/test_rate_limit.py (create); docs/guides/usage-queries.md (create); docs/decisions/provider-spend-limit.md (create); apps/api/app/generation/jobs.py (modify) |
| Implementation | 1. Implement an in-memory sliding-window limiter in rate_limit.py keyed by user id and client address, limit RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN (60); apply as a dependency to API-16, API-22, API-25 to API-31; on excess return 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After header and retry_after_s (§6 envelope).<br>2. In generation/service.py, before creating the ai_generations row, count today's (UTC) rows for the user and globally excluding model_id rule_based_planner_v1 (reference operation 1, §5); if >= AI_DAILY_GENERATIONS_PER_USER or AI_DAILY_GENERATIONS_GLOBAL return 429 AI_QUOTA_REACHED with the next UTC midnight as reset time; never call the provider.<br>3. Add the daily purge of ai_generations rows whose retention_until has passed (90 days, OD-10) to the scheduler in app/generation/jobs.py; linked generation ids become null (IMD-31).<br>4. When the global cap is reached, the error details tell the client that mode rule_based is available; the generate page offers a "Build a rule-based plan" button that calls API-22 with mode rule_based (not counted against the cap).<br>5. Apply AI_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS / AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS in limits.py (request builder trims the shortlist; adapter sets max output tokens) when set.<br>6. Document the daily-count query in docs/guides/usage-queries.md and the provider-side spending/quota limit chosen at setup (owner Kirtan, status Awaiting validation until set) in docs/decisions/provider-spend-limit.md. |
| Interfaces | API: API-22, API-16, API-25, API-26, API-27, API-28, API-29, API-30, API-31 · Tables: ai_generations · Modules: MOD-B01, MOD-B05, MOD-B06 · Env: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN, AI_DAILY_GENERATIONS_PER_USER, AI_DAILY_GENERATIONS_GLOBAL, AI_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS, AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS · Other: error codes RATE_LIMITED, AI_QUOTA_REACHED |

| Task | Sprint 6 (week 6) · CODE · 8 points · lead Het with Junaid, Manasvi · release EXT · Extension; switch optimise_order (cut 6 of 9). When disabled the traveller still reorders by drag or keyboard (API-26). |

| Owners and parts | Het (lead) — Preview and apply endpoints (API-66, API-67) as one edit (3 points)<br>Junaid — Ordering heuristic (nearest neighbour + 2-opt) over the travel-time matrix (3 points)<br>Manasvi — Optimise button and before/after preview dialog (2 points)<br>One branch and pull request per part (`feat/IMP-612-<part>`); the backend, database or AI part merges first |
| Traces to | Stories US-157; FR-130; NFR-003 |
| Dependencies | Prerequisites: IMP-407, IMP-307, IMP-506, IMP-606 · Downstream: IMP-699 |
| Files | apps/api/app/itinerary/optimise.py (create); apps/api/app/itinerary/router.py (modify); apps/api/app/itinerary/service.py (modify); apps/api/app/itinerary/schemas.py (modify); apps/web/components/itinerary/OptimiseDayDialog.tsx (create); apps/web/components/itinerary/DayColumn.tsx (modify); apps/api/tests/unit/itinerary/test_optimise.py (create); apps/api/tests/api/test_optimise.py (create); apps/web/tests/unit/itinerary/OptimiseDayDialog.test.tsx (create); contracts/openapi.v1.json (modify) |
| Implementation | 1. Contract first: on day 1 of the sprint the API part declares this card's endpoints with their final shapes (§6) and regenerates contracts/openapi.v1.json with make openapi; handlers return 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED until built (IMD-37: allowed for extension routes until SG-7), so the screen part starts against the regenerated web client (Team Contribution Plan v2).<br>2. Implement app/itinerary/optimise.py (pure): split the day into segments between locked items and fixed meal slots; within each segment order unlocked items by nearest neighbour from the segment start, then improve with 2-opt; travel minutes come from a matrix built by the routing service (route_cache first, fallback estimate otherwise; no new external call per permutation).<br>3. Keep a proposal only if total travel falls by at least 5 minutes and recalculation plus validation adds no new error finding (OVERLAP, CLOSED_ON_DAY, OUTSIDE_HOURS, UNKNOWN_PLACE, OUTSIDE_TRIP_DATES); otherwise return status no_better_order (or nothing_to_optimise with fewer than three movable items), as OptimisePreviewOut in §6.5.1.<br>4. Implement API-66 GET .../days/{day_number}/optimise (preview, no write): proposed order, travel minutes before and after, findings after the change, plan_revision it is based on.<br>5. Implement API-67 POST .../days/{day_number}/optimise with body OptimiseApplyIn {plan_revision, item_ids}: verify item_ids are exactly the day's items with locked items and meal slots in their positions (else 422 INVALID_EDIT), then apply as one edit transaction through the edit core (recalculate, revalidate, automatic version reason edit, IMD-18); stale revision 409 STALE_PLAN; active generation 409 GENERATION_IN_PROGRESS (IMD-23).<br>6. Build OptimiseDayDialog: "Optimise order" button in DayColumn header opens the preview with before/after list and minutes saved; Apply calls API-67 and replaces the plan with the response; "No better order found" when status is no_better_order or nothing_to_optimise.<br>7. Add the switch: Guard with the extension switch 'optimise_order' (IMD-11, EXT): when FEATURES_DISABLED / NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURES_DISABLED contains 'optimise_order' the routes return 404 NOT_FOUND and the UI entry point is hidden (TC-432). |

Implement app/context/client.py (only MediaWiki HTTP here): Wikivoyage page by destination title first, Wikipedia second; places by exact title or GeoData geosearch within 100 m of the stored coordinates; TextExtracts intro as plain text; descriptive WIKI_USER_AGENT header; serial requests; timeout; strip to 1,200 chars on a sentence boundary.<br>4. Implement jobs.py: refresh cards older than 30 days for active places and destinations, one request at a time, registered in the existing scheduler; on-demand reads never call MediaWiki (cache only).<br>5. Implement API-72 GET /api/v1/places/{place_id}/context and API-73 GET /api/v1/destinations/{destination_id}/context returning the card with title, extract, source, licence, page_url and retrieved_at, or 404 when none.<br>6. Build ContextCard in PlaceDetailDrawer and the destination header: "From Wikivoyage/Wikipedia" label, licence and link, retrieved date; never shown in place of curated prices or hours.<br>7. Add the switch: Guard with the extension switch 'context_cards' (IMD-11, EXT): when FEATURES_DISABLED / NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURES_DISABLED contains 'context_cards' the routes return 404 NOT_FOUND and the UI entry point is hidden (TC-432). Startup check: WIKI_USER_AGENT must be set in staging and production when the switch is on. Tests mock MediaWiki with respx. |

# 11. Exact instructions for Claude Code

This section is the operating procedure for every Claude Code session on the project. It is also published as `docs/spec/SPRINT_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`; the prompts that start a session are in §12.2 and §12.3.

## 11.1 Inputs Claude Code reads, in this order

| Order | Input | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `CLAUDE.md` (§12.1) | Stack, layout, rules, commands, Definition of Done |
| 2 | The task card in `docs/spec/TASK_REGISTER.md` (same content as §10) | Objective, prerequisites, files, steps, interfaces, acceptance criteria, tests, evidence |
| 3 | The contract sections the card's interfaces name: §3 (module), §5 (tables), §6 (endpoints), §7 (screens), §8 and §9 (AI and deterministic rules), §13 (tests) | The shapes that must not change |
| 4 | `docs/progress/parts/` (one record per merged part), `docs/progress/sprint-N.md` (sprint index) and `docs/progress/gates.md` | What is done, blocked or waiting |
| 5 | `docs/spec/DECISION_REGISTER.md` | Provisional defaults and any decision that changed a contract |
| 6 | The repository itself: the files the card lists and their neighbours, existing tests, `Makefile`, `.env.example` | What already exists; never assume |

## 11.2 Procedure for one task

1. **Receive.** The run prompt (written by the planner, Appendix D) names one run ID, one task ID, the part to build (the card's "Owners and parts" row), the member who owns it with their git name and email, and the reviewer. Read the card and the inputs of §11.1. Restate the objective, the part's scope and the acceptance criteria it must satisfy in two or three lines.
2. **Check prerequisites.** Every prerequisite task must be `done` in `docs/progress/`; every named contract must exist in the code or the specification. If one is missing, stop and report a blocker (§11.5); do not build the missing piece unless it is a trivial, clearly implied part of this task. A prerequisite that is an extension or cut-list feature switched off by a recorded decision counts as satisfied for gate and test cards, which skip its checks with the reason; when an extension card needs a shared piece of a switched-off extension (the assist-call log of IMP-613), it builds that piece itself as IMD-60 says.
3. **Inspect.** List the files the card names and confirm which exist. Read existing code in the module, its tests and the shared schemas before writing. If the repository structure differs from §4, follow the repository and report the difference.
4. **Detect conflicts.** Compare the card with the code and the contracts. A conflict (a different field name, a missing table, an endpoint that already returns another shape) is reported before coding, with a proposed resolution. Small, obviously compatible additions (an extra index, a helper) are allowed and listed in the report.
5. **Plan.** Write a short plan: files to create or modify, in order; tests to write first or alongside.
6. **Implement.** Follow the card's steps in order, limited to the named part on a shared card; another member's part is used through its contract (stub, generated client or MOCK) and is never built in its place. Reuse existing modules, schemas, error codes, labels and names. Write real behaviour, not placeholders: no TODO stubs in code paths the acceptance criteria exercise.
7. **Test.** Write or update the tests the card lists. Run, in this order, the card's test commands, then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make imports`, then `make test` (and `make openapi-check` if the API changed, `make e2e` if a journey changed). Fix every failure your change caused; re-run until green.
8. **Verify the criteria.** Walk through each acceptance criterion and point to the test or observation that shows it. A criterion that needs something unavailable (a real key, a deployed URL, a human session) is marked "not verified" with the reason.
9. **Record and commit.** Create the part record `docs/progress/parts/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>.md` (run ID, owner, status, base commit, changed files, commands with their result lines, acceptance criteria with verified or not verified, blockers, proposed decisions, open issues). Blockers and proposed decisions are recorded there and in the SYNC REPORT only; the decision register is changed by a separate decision run once the team has decided. Commit as the part owner (CLAUDE.md §12), run the two attribution checks, push the branch and open the pull request with the owner as assignee and the named reviewer. Never merge.
10. **Report and stop.** Print the SYNC REPORT of §11.4 and stop at the part boundary. Do not start another part.

## 11.3 Rules that apply to every task

- Implement only the selected task and what it strictly needs. Do not refactor unrelated code, rename public items, or rewrite modules from scratch.
- Never change a contract silently: endpoints, request and response shapes, tables and columns, finding and error codes, labels, environment variable names, file layout and commands are changed only through a reported proposal and, once approved, in the same pull request as the specification registers.
- Never report a test as passing unless it ran and passed in this session (or in a CI run you can link). Quote the command and its summary line. "Should pass" is not evidence.
- Never fabricate data: no invented prices, hours, places, routes, evaluation numbers, user findings or screenshots. SAMPLE fixtures are labelled SAMPLE everywhere.
- Never call Gemini in automated tests; use MOCK scenarios or recorded responses. Never print or commit secrets.
- When a decision is genuinely open and blocks the task, apply the Provisional default from Appendix B if one exists; otherwise stop and report.

## 11.4 Report format at the end of a run: the SYNC REPORT

Every run ends with the SYNC REPORT block defined in `CLAUDE.md` §14 (reproduced in Appendix D.4), printed exactly, so that the planner can check it and update its ledger. It carries the run, card, part and owner; the status (`PR_OPEN`, `BLOCKED`, `TESTS_FAILING`, `PARTIAL`, `NO_CHANGE`); the branch, base and head commits; every commit with its author and committer; the result of the attribution check; the pull request and reviewer; the changed files, contracts and migrations; each command with its exact result line; the commands not run and why; each acceptance criterion with verified or not verified and how; blockers; proposed decisions; and the path of the part record.

## 11.5 Blockers

A blocker is reported, not worked around, when: a prerequisite task is not done; a contract in the card contradicts the code or another section; an account, key, dataset or human decision is missing; or the task cannot meet an acceptance criterion without changing scope. The report names the blocker, what was done up to that point, and the smallest decision or input that would unblock it. Partial work is committed only if it leaves `make check` green and is marked `blocked` in its part record.

## 11.6 Procedure for a sprint

A sprint is driven by the planner (Appendix D), one part per Claude Code run; Claude Code is never asked to run a whole sprint unattended.

1. **Start.** The planner reads the sprint section of §10, its gate in §14, the dependency map and the sprint's column of the team load table (§14.3), and confirms that the previous gate is recorded as passed or that its open items have owners.
2. **Order.** Parts run in an order that respects prerequisites (§14.2 lists the waves); the backend, database or AI part of a card comes before its screen part. CODE parts are implemented by Claude Code; DATA, HUMAN and VERIFY parts are prepared by Claude Code (imports, checks, templates, checklists) and closed by the named member with evidence.
3. **Per part.** One run applies §11.2: one branch `feat|fix|chore/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>`, commits authored by the part's owner, one part record, one pull request titled like `IMP-409 · move-controls part`, then the SYNC REPORT. The named reviewer approves and the operator merges with Rebase and merge.
4. **Integrate.** After each merge `make check` on `main` must stay green; a red `main` stops new parts until the owner of the breaking change fixes it.
5. **Close.** The gate card (IMP-N99, or the gate task named in §14) compiles `docs/progress/sprint-N.md` from the part records, checks each gate criterion with evidence in `docs/progress/gates.md`, and moves unfinished parts, with a reason, to the next sprint or the deferred list. A sprint is never complete because code was generated; it is complete when the application builds, the relevant tests ran and passed, and the integrated behaviour was verified.

## 11.7 Planner and executor

The implementation is run by two assistants kept in step through the repository. A planner (a Claude chat that holds this specification, the task register, the decision register and the team plan) writes one prompt per part; Claude Code executes it in the repository and ends with the SYNC REPORT; the operator carries the prompt in one direction and the report in the other, approves through the reviewer and merges. The repository is the source of truth: merged pull requests and the part records in `docs/progress/parts/` decide what is done, and a read-only RESYNC run rebuilds the planner's ledger from them whenever the two disagree. The full protocol, its diagrams and the planner prompt are in Appendix D.

# 12. Root CLAUDE.md and prompt templates

## 12.1 Root `CLAUDE.md`

The file below is committed at the repository root by IMP-101 and kept current by every task that changes a rule, command or path. It is deliberately short, because Claude Code loads it into every session; it points to this specification for detail. The same text is delivered as the standalone file `CLAUDE.md`.

~~~~markdown
# CLAUDE.md — AI Travel Planner

Read this file at the start of every session. It is short on purpose; the binding details live in the implementation specification, `docs/spec/IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md` (sections cited as §N; search it by heading, for example `## 6.6`). When this file and the specification disagree, the specification wins; report the disagreement.

## 1. Project in one paragraph

A web app where a signed-in traveller describes a trip and gets a day-wise, costed, editable itinerary. Gemini proposes the plan from a shortlist of curated places; the backend validates every place ID, recalculates every time, travel gap and price in code, labels every estimate and saves the plan with its warnings. When Gemini fails, a rule-based planner produces a labelled plan. Eight one-week sprints, ten students. The MVP scope is the requirement register (§2). Nine extensions (release code EXT, §2.5) are built in Sprints 5 to 7 by their own cards, each behind a switch, and are switched off before any MVP feature if time runs short. Anything marked T1, R2, PP or Stage 2 is not built unless a task card says so. In-app flight and hotel booking, payments and live prices are excluded (IMD-46): never add a booking provider, payment flow or booking claim.

## 2. Stack (do not replace)

- Web: Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, dnd-kit, TanStack Query, react-hook-form + zod, MapLibre GL JS + OpenFreeMap, openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch.
- API: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, pydantic-settings, SQLAlchemy 2 async with psycopg 3, Alembic (runs versioned SQL files).
- Data and auth: Supabase Postgres and Supabase Auth; Supabase CLI local stack for development.
- AI: Gemini through `google-genai`, only behind `ModelProvider`; adapters GEMINI, MOCK, FINETUNED_MODEL (stub in Stage 1).
- Routing: OpenRouteService with cache and distance fallback. Hosting: Vercel (web), Render (API container). CI: GitHub Actions.
- Tests: pytest, Vitest + Testing Library, Playwright + axe. Quality: ruff, mypy, import-linter, ESLint, Prettier, pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks.

Adding a dependency needs a reason in the pull request; adding a framework, service, queue or database needs a decision in `docs/spec/DECISION_REGISTER.md` first.

## 3. Where things live

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/api/app/<module>/` | Backend modules: core, auth, trips, places, ai, generation, validation, itinerary, budget, routing, evaluation, and the extension modules prep (packing only), weather and context; each with router.py, service.py, repository.py, schemas.py and, for pure rules, domain or engine files |
| `apps/api/app/schemas/` | Shared contracts: `ai.py` (gr-1, io-1, ProviderResult, findings), `common.py` (Money, Page, error envelope), `labels.py` |
| `apps/api/app/db/models/` | ORM models mirroring the SQL migrations, one file per owning module |
| `apps/api/migrations/sql/` and `versions/` | Schema source of truth (SQL) and the Alembic revisions that execute it |
| `apps/api/tests/` | unit/, contract/, api/, authz/, smoke/, fixtures/ |
| `apps/web/app/` | Routes: `(public)/` landing, sign-in, sign-up; `(app)/` dashboard, profile, trips/... |
| `apps/web/components/<area>/`, `apps/web/lib/` | Components by area; API client, query hooks, auth, formatting, zod schemas |
| `apps/web/tests/unit/`, `apps/web/e2e/` | Vitest component tests; Playwright specs |
| `contracts/` | Generated `openapi.v1.json` and AI JSON Schemas (committed, never edited by hand) |
| `data/fixtures/sampleton/`, `data/places/<slug>/` | SAMPLE test destination; curated destinations |
| `docs/spec/` | The specification (`IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md`), the registers (TASK_REGISTER, DECISION_REGISTER, TRACEABILITY_MATRIX), SPRINT_EXECUTION_GUIDE, ORCHESTRATOR_PROMPT and `sql/` (the reference migrations of Appendix A); placed by the operator and committed unchanged in IMP-101 |
| `docs/progress/sprint-N.md`, `docs/progress/gates.md` | Task status and evidence; gate results |

## 4. Architecture rules (enforced by `make imports` and review)

1. Backend layers: routers → services → domain and repositories → clients and adapters. Routers hold no business rules and no SQL. Domain code does no I/O and imports no FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, HTTP client or SDK.
2. `google-genai` is imported only in `app/ai/providers/gemini.py`; only `app/ai/factory.py` imports concrete adapters; OpenRouteService HTTP calls only in `app/routing/client.py`; Open-Meteo calls only in `app/weather/client.py`; MediaWiki calls only in `app/context/client.py` (from its background job, with `WIKI_USER_AGENT`).
3. One writer per table: only the owning module writes its tables (§3); other modules call its service.
4. The user ID comes only from the verified token (`CurrentUser` dependency) and is passed to every repository query. A resource that exists but belongs to someone else returns 404 `NOT_FOUND`, never 403.
5. The browser never queries the database, never holds a provider, routing or database secret, and never computes prices, totals, times or travel gaps; it displays what the API returns.
6. No circular imports between modules; shared types go in `app/schemas/` (backend) or `lib/` (web).

## 5. Commands (run from the repository root)

| Purpose | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install everything | `make setup` |
| Local Supabase stack (auth + Postgres) / plain test Postgres | `make stack-up`, `make stack-down` / `make db-up`, `make db-down` |
| Apply migrations / reset local data / load seed data | `make db-migrate` / `make db-reset` (local and test only) / `make seed` |
| Run API (port 8000) / web (port 3000) | `make api` / `make web` |
| Lint / types / import boundaries | `make lint` / `make typecheck` / `make imports` |
| Tests | `make test-unit`, `make test-contract`, `make test-api`, `make test-authz`, `make test-web`, `make test` (all except E2E) |
| End-to-end (MOCK provider, local stack) | `make e2e` (filter with `ARGS='--grep <tag>'`) |
| API contract and AI schemas | `make openapi` after any API or schema change; `make openapi-check` must pass |
| Everything a pull request needs | `make check` |
| Evaluation / deployed smoke / live Gemini check | `make eval PROVIDER=MOCK DATASET=<version>` / `make smoke URL=<base url>` / `make live-smoke` (only with a key, never in PR CI) |

`ARGS` passes extra arguments to the wrapped tool (pytest `-k name`, vitest or Playwright filters, seed `--check --strict`). If a command does not exist yet, the task that creates it is in `docs/spec/TASK_REGISTER.md`; do not invent a different command.

## 6. Environment variables

- Names and placeholders are in `.env.example` only; real values live in untracked `apps/api/.env`, `apps/web/.env.local`, the hosting dashboards and the CI secret store.
- Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURES_DISABLED` may reach the browser.
- `AI_PROVIDER` is MOCK in local and test, GEMINI in staging and production. The API refuses to start in staging or production if a required `GEMINI_*` value is empty or a placeholder, or if production uses MOCK.
- Never print, log, commit or paste a key, a token, a connection string, a prompt body or personal data. Do not set `GOOGLE_API_KEY`.

## 7. Database and API rules

- Schema changes only through a new migration pair (`migrations/sql/NNNN_name.sql` + `versions/NNNN_name.py`), one per pull request; never edit a merged migration; keep one Alembic head; update the ORM models in the same change; `tests/api/test_schema_drift.py` must pass.
- Tables are only those of the MVP migrations 0001 to 0006 and the extension migrations 0007 to 0010 (§5), each extension migration created by its own card. Do not create T1 or R2 tables.
- API under `/api/v1`, JSON snake_case, UUID identifiers, dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, times `HH:MM` in the destination time zone, timestamps UTC ISO 8601, money as two-decimal strings with a currency code, the error envelope of §6.3 for every error, `plan_revision` on every itinerary read and edit.
- One request and response shape per operation, defined once in the module's `schemas.py`; regenerate `contracts/openapi.v1.json` and the web types in the same pull request.
- Every edit is one transaction that recalculates and revalidates; generation results are saved in one transaction (plan, warnings, version, record).

## 8. AI provider and security rules

- The model may only choose place IDs from the shortlist it was given, their order and times, and short notes. Prices, opening hours, travel times, totals and availability always come from data and code. Model output is parsed into `ItineraryOutput` (io-1) and validated; it never builds SQL, never names a table or user, and is never executed.
- Unknown place IDs, schema failures, timeouts, rate limits, quota and configuration errors follow the error taxonomy (§8): at most the configured retries, at most one repair call, then the labelled rule-based fallback; quota and configuration errors end in `failed` with a rule-based option. Every generation writes its record.
- Tests never call Gemini. Use the MOCK adapter (`MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO`) or recorded responses in `tests/fixtures/provider_recordings/`. Live calls only through `make live-smoke` with an explicit key.
- The three assistive operations (`extract_trip_request`, `explain_day`, `suggest_packing_items`) follow the same rule: the model proposes, code validates every value (trip and preference validators, places on the day, fixed packing vocabulary); each call is written to `ai_assist_calls` and counted against `AI_DAILY_ASSIST_CALLS_PER_USER`; nothing is saved from intake until the traveller confirms (§8.20).
- No private user data is used for training or evaluation datasets (PD-09). No Stage 2 work without a recorded decision.

## 9. Testing expectations

- Write or update tests in the same change as the code; each task card names its test files, TC IDs and command.
- Unit tests for domain rules (validation, budget, ranking, scheduling, fallback); API tests with a real migrated PostgreSQL; an authorization test for every new owned route; contract tests for every adapter; component tests for every new interactive component; E2E for journeys.
- Never report a test as passing unless it ran in this session or in CI and passed; paste the command and the summary line. If a test cannot run (missing Docker, key or account), say so and mark the evidence as missing.
- Do not delete, skip or weaken a failing test to get green; fix the code or report the conflict. Skips are allowed only for disabled cut-list features or extensions (switched off in `FEATURES_DISABLED`) and `live` tests without a key.

## 10. Prohibited shortcuts

- Hard-coded itineraries, prices, hours, routes, success messages or "fake" API responses in production code (fixtures and MOCK scenarios live only in test and mock paths and are labelled SAMPLE).
- Building an extension without its switch (IMD-47); a switched-off extension hides its screens and its routes return 404.
- Calling Gemini, ORS, Open-Meteo or MediaWiki from the browser; secrets in code, tests or fixtures; disabling auth, CORS or RLS to make something work.
- Catch-all exception handlers that hide errors; `# type: ignore`, `any` or `eslint-disable` without a one-line reason.
- Changing an API shape, table, finding code, error code or environment variable name without updating the specification registers and the contract files in the same pull request.
- Rewriting working modules that the task does not name; large refactors without a task.

## 11. Definition of Done for a task part

1. The task's acceptance criteria hold and are shown by the listed tests.
2. `make check` passes locally or in CI; `make e2e` passes when the task touches a journey.
3. OpenAPI and web types regenerated if the API changed; migrations and drift test updated if the schema changed.
4. No new lint, type or import-boundary violations; no secrets; labels and error states present on new screens.
5. The part record `docs/progress/parts/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>.md` is created in the same pull request: run id, owner, status, base commit (not its own head commit: Rebase and merge changes commit IDs), changed files, the commands run with their result lines, each acceptance criterion with verified or not verified and how, blockers, proposed decisions and open issues. `docs/progress/sprint-N.md` is the sprint index; the gate card compiles it from the part records. The card's lead marks the card done when all its parts are merged and its acceptance criteria are verified.
6. The pull request uses the template, cites the IMP task, the part and the requirement IDs, is titled like `IMP-409 · move-controls part`, is assigned to the part owner, names the reviewer (§12) and gets one approval before it is merged with Rebase and merge.

## 12. Team, identity, branches and pull requests

- Ten members own 427 points of the 108 cards, 42 or 43 each (Team Contribution Plan version 2, specification §14.3 and Appendix C). Every card names its lead and its parts in the "Owners and parts" row. Build only the part the prompt names, and use other parts through their contracts.
- **Commit identity.** Every commit of a part is authored and committed as the part's owner, with the git name and email given in the run prompt. Pass them to every git command that writes history: `git -c user.name="<name>" -c user.email="<email>" commit -m "<message>"`, and the same `-c` pair for `commit --amend`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert` and `merge`. Never set `user.name` or `user.email` in any git config (global or repository), never use `--author` alone, and never rewrite commits already on `main` or made by another member. Rebasing your part's branch on `main` is done with the owner's `-c` pair and pushed with `git push --force-with-lease`, only on that branch and only before the pull request is approved.
- **One author per commit.** No `Co-authored-by:` line of any kind. No commit message, branch name, pull request title or body, or code comment mentions Claude, Claude Code or Anthropic, or says that an AI assistant wrote or helped with the work; the paths `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/` are the exceptions. The project documents already in the repository (`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/spec/`) stay as they are, and nothing new states who or what wrote the code. The product's own AI features (Gemini, ModelProvider, "AI-written" labels) are product content, not attribution. The tracked `commit-msg` hook in `.githooks/` and the CI job `attribution` enforce this (IMP-102); `.claude/settings.json` sets `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` (IMP-101).
- **Before pushing**, run both checks and fix only your own new commits if one fails:
  `git log origin/main..HEAD --format='%h|%an|%ae|%cn|%ce|%s'` (only the owner's name and email, as author and committer) and
  `git log origin/main..HEAD --format='%B' | perl -ne 's/CLAUDE\.md|\.claude\///gi; print if /co-authored-by|anthropic|\bclaude\b/i'` (prints nothing).
- One branch per part: `feat|fix|chore/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>` (for example `feat/IMP-409-move-api`, `feat/IMP-409-move-controls`). The backend, database or AI part merges before the screen part that uses it. Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and start with the task ID, for example `feat(itinerary): IMP-409 keyboard move controls`.
- Pull requests are opened with `gh pr create`, assigned to the part owner, with the reviewer named in the run prompt, who is never the operator who opens the pull request and never the part owner (the planner chooses the card's lead, else the owner of the largest other part, else the CODEOWNERS owner, else the review pair). The pull-request body is written to a temporary file outside the repository. Claude Code never merges, never pushes to `main` and never force-pushes an approved branch.
- Merging uses **Rebase and merge** only (merge commits and squash merging are disabled in the repository settings), so every commit keeps its author and each merged part stays credited to its owner; on `main` GitHub records its own committer, which is expected. Kirtan is the integration lead: he keeps `main` green and resolves migration heads and contract conflicts.

## 13. Working with the specification

- Before changing any contract (endpoint, schema, table, code, env var, file layout), read the relevant section (§3 to §9). If the change is needed, stop and report it as a proposed decision instead of making it silently.
- Work one part at a time from `docs/spec/TASK_REGISTER.md`; confirm its prerequisites are merged on `main` (their part records exist in `docs/progress/parts/`); implement only that part; stop at its boundary.
- Record blockers and proposed decisions in the part record and the SYNC REPORT only, with the reason and what is needed. The gate card writes them into `docs/progress/`, and a separate decision run updates `docs/spec/DECISION_REGISTER.md` once the team has decided.

## 14. SYNC REPORT (end of every run)

Every run ends with this block, printed exactly, so the planner can update its ledger (specification Appendix D). Use `none` or `[]` for empty fields; never omit a field; quote command result lines exactly.

```text
<<<SYNC-REPORT
run_id: RUN-…
card: IMP-…
part: <part-slug>
owner: <Member>
status: PR_OPEN | BLOCKED | TESTS_FAILING | PARTIAL | NO_CHANGE
branch: <name or none>
base_commit: <sha>
head_commit: <sha or none>
commits:
  - <sha7> | <author name> <author email> | <committer name> <committer email> | <subject>
attribution_check: PASS | FAIL (<what>)
pr: <url or none>
reviewer_requested: <github user or none>
files_changed: [<paths>]
contracts_changed: none | [<what, and the proposal ID>]
migrations_added: none | [<file>]
commands:
  - cmd: <command>
    result: <exact summary line>
not_run:
  - cmd: <command>
    reason: <why>
acceptance:
  - criterion: <FR/TC id or text>
    status: verified | not verified
    how: <test or observation>
blockers: [<text>]
proposed_decisions: [<text>]
part_record: docs/progress/parts/<IMP-NNN>-<part-slug>.md
SYNC-REPORT>>>
```
~~~~

## 12.2 Prompt template: one run (one task part)

The planner fills this template for every run (Appendix D); every field comes from the card, the team table and the specification. It is used for every CODE part and for the preparation part of DATA, HUMAN and VERIFY parts.

```text
=== RUN <RUN-ID> · <IMP-NNN> <card title> · part: <part-slug> (<points> pts) · Sprint <N>, wave <W> · <NEW | FIX of RUN-xxx | CONTINUE step k of n> ===

You are working on the AI Travel Planner repository as <Member>, <Role title>. Everything you commit in this run is authored and committed by <Member>.

IDENTITY (pass it to every git command that writes history; never set user.name or user.email in git config):
  GIT_NAME="<Git author name>"   GIT_EMAIL="<Git author email>"   GITHUB_USER="<github-username>"
  Commit:  git -c user.name="$GIT_NAME" -c user.email="$GIT_EMAIL" commit -m "<message>"
  Rebase:  git -c user.name="$GIT_NAME" -c user.email="$GIT_EMAIL" rebase origin/main   (then git push --force-with-lease, only on this branch and only before approval)
  No Co-authored-by lines. No mention of Claude, Claude Code or Anthropic, and no statement that an AI wrote or helped, in commits, branch, PR title or body or code comments (the paths CLAUDE.md and .claude/ are fine).

READ FIRST: CLAUDE.md · docs/spec/TASK_REGISTER.md card <IMP-NNN> (copy its steps, acceptance criteria and test commands from there, exactly) · docs/spec/IMPLEMENTATION_SPEC.md <§ list from the card's interfaces> · docs/spec/DECISION_REGISTER.md <IMD list if relevant> · docs/progress/parts/ (records of the prerequisites)

PREFLIGHT (stop with status BLOCKED and the SYNC REPORT if any check fails):
  1. git fetch origin; git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no prints nothing (untracked files are fine). Record the base commit: git rev-parse --short origin/main.
  2. Prerequisites are merged on main: <for each prerequisite: IMP-NNN part — the concrete evidence to check, e.g. its part record docs/progress/parts/IMP-NNN-<slug>.md or a file path that must exist>.
  3. Attribution guard: if .githooks/commit-msg exists, run git config core.hooksPath .githooks; otherwise make sure the local guard from RUN-000 is in .git/hooks/commit-msg.
  4. Branch: NEW run: git switch main && git pull --ff-only && git switch -c <feat|fix|chore>/<IMP-NNN>-<part-slug>. FIX or CONTINUE run: git switch <existing branch> && git pull --ff-only, and rebase on origin/main as IDENTITY says if the pull request shows a conflict.

YOUR PART (build only this): "<part text from Owners and parts>"   (a single-owner card uses the slug whole-task)
Other parts of this card belong to <members>; use them only through their contracts (generated client, stubs, MOCK). Do not create or edit their files: <list>.

FILES: <create/modify list from the card, limited to this part>
STEPS: the card's steps <numbers> that belong to this part, taken from the task register; <for a step shared with another part: which half is this part's and which member does the other half>
CONTRACTS THAT MUST NOT CHANGE: <endpoints, schemas, tables, codes, env vars this part touches, with § refs>
ACCEPTANCE (this part's share of the card): <criterion IDs: FR-xxx ACn, TC-xxx, and the card's criteria by number>
TESTS TO WRITE AND RUN: the card's test files and commands for this part; then make lint, make typecheck, make imports, make test<, make openapi-check if the API changed><, make e2e ARGS='--grep <tag>' if a journey changed>.
EVIDENCE: create docs/progress/parts/<IMP-NNN>-<part-slug>.md with: run id, owner, status, base commit, files changed, commands run with their result lines, acceptance criteria with verified/not verified and how, blockers and proposed decisions, open issues. Do not edit docs/progress/sprint-N.md or the decision register in a part run.

COMMITS (suggested): <2-6 Conventional Commit messages starting with IMP-NNN>
BEFORE PUSH: run the two attribution checks of CLAUDE.md §12 and repair your own new commits if needed.
PUSH AND PR (NEW run; a FIX or CONTINUE run only pushes, except the last CONTINUE step, which opens the PR):
  git push -u origin <branch>
  write the PR body to a temporary file outside the repository (BODY=$(mktemp)) from .github/pull_request_template.md when it exists: linked IDs, what changed, tests run with results, screenshots for UI, contract changed?, migration?, part owner and reviewer
  gh pr create --base main --head <branch> --title "<IMP-NNN> · <part-slug> part" --assignee <owner GitHub user> --reviewer <reviewer GitHub user> --body-file "$BODY"
  Do not merge.

STOP CONDITIONS: a prerequisite missing; a contract conflict; a needed account, key or dataset missing; acceptance impossible without changing scope; main red for reasons outside this part. In each case stop, keep make check green on your branch (or commit nothing), and report.

FINISH: print the SYNC REPORT exactly in the format of CLAUDE.md §14 and stop. Do not start another part.
```

## 12.3 Prompt template: read-only state check (RESYNC)

Sprints are not run in one Claude Code session; the planner issues one run per part (§11.6). When the planner's ledger and the repository may disagree, it issues this read-only prompt and rebuilds its ledger from the STATE REPORT.

```text
=== RESYNC · read-only state dump (no commits, no edits) ===
In the repository root, run git fetch --all --prune, then print a STATE REPORT:
<<<STATE-REPORT
main_head: <sha> <date> <subject>
merged_parts: one line per docs/progress/parts/*.md on main: <file> | owner | status
main_commits_by_author: git shortlog -sne origin/main
recent_main: git log origin/main -n 40 --format='%h|%an|%ae|%s'
open_prs: gh pr list --state open --json number,title,headRefName,author,assignees,reviewRequests,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup (one line each)
merged_prs_last_50: gh pr list --state merged -L 50 --json number,title,mergedAt (one line each)
alembic_heads: (cd apps/api && alembic heads) or "not available yet"
checks: result line of make check on main, or the reason it cannot run
STATE-REPORT>>>
Stop after printing.
```

## 12.4 Keeping instructions and specification in step

| Change | Update in the same pull request |
| --- | --- |
| New or changed command | `Makefile`, `CLAUDE.md` §5, §4 of this specification, README |
| New environment variable | `.env.example`, settings class and start-up checks, `CLAUDE.md` §6, §4.5 |
| API change | `contracts/openapi.v1.json`, web types, §6 entry, TASK_REGISTER card if open |
| Schema change | New migration pair, ORM models, drift test, §5 and Appendix A |
| New decision | `docs/spec/DECISION_REGISTER.md` entry, status Proposed until the team approves |
| Part finished | Its part record in `docs/progress/parts/` (the gate card compiles `docs/progress/sprint-N.md`); TRACEABILITY_MATRIX if files or tests differ from the card |
| Owner or part changed | The card's "Owners and parts" row, Appendix C, the board issue and §14.3 load table, regenerated from the team data; agreed at sprint planning; the planner's team table and ledger |
| Run protocol or SYNC REPORT changed | `CLAUDE.md` §12 and §14, §11, Appendix D and `docs/spec/ORCHESTRATOR_PROMPT.md` together |

# 13. Testing and verification

This section says which tests exist, where they live, how they run and what counts as evidence. The full test specifications (TC-001 to TC-398, groups G1 to G12) stay in blueprint §28; the extension cases TC-399 to TC-432 (EXT) are defined by the cards of IMP-515, IMP-612, IMP-613 and IMP-708 to IMP-713 and listed for addition to blueprint §28; the cards of §10 name the TC IDs each task implements. **No test has been run yet.** The only executed checks so far are the MVP DDL load and the reference operations on a scratch PostgreSQL 16.15 (§5). Every threshold below is Proposed.

## 13.1 Rules

| Rule | What it means in practice |
| --- | --- |
| Tests are written with the code | A task is not done until the tests named in its card exist and pass. A bug fix adds a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it. |
| Never report a test as passing unless it ran | A result is reported only from an actual run: the command, its exit code and the summary line (for example `42 passed, 1 skipped`). A skipped test is reported as skipped, with the reason. Do not count a test as passed because it was written or because it is "expected to pass". |
| Mock and live are different results | Automated runs use the `MOCK` provider, recorded provider responses or mocked HTTP. A live call (real Gemini or OpenRouteService) is marked `live`, skipped when the key is absent, never runs in pull-request CI, and is reported separately as "live". A mock result is never presented as evidence about Gemini. |
| No credential without a mock path | Every test that touches an external service has a mock or recorded variant that runs with no key. Pull-request CI holds no provider key. A socket guard in `tests/conftest.py` fails any test that opens a network connection to a provider host unless it is marked `live`. |
| Synthetic data only | Tests use the Sampleton fixture (§13.6), generated users and generated trips. No real personal data, no real keys, no prompt bodies from real users. |
| Evidence is recorded | Each task's checklist line in `docs/progress/sprint-N.md` links the CI run (or pastes the command and the summary line for a local run) and, for UI tasks, a screenshot. Gate results go to `docs/progress/gates.md` (§14). Manual checks (live smoke, usability, real devices) are recorded with date, person, environment and outcome. |
| Disabled features | A cut-list feature switched off with `FEATURES_DISABLED` (IMD-11) has its tests skipped with the reason "disabled by cut-list decision"; the floor journey (TC-372) must still pass. An extension switched off (EXT switch names, §4.5) has its tests skipped with the reason "extension <switch> disabled", except TC-432, which checks that its UI is hidden and its endpoints return 404. |
| Extension services offline | Open-Meteo and MediaWiki are reached only through respx mocks with recorded JSON; the socket guard also blocks `api.open-meteo.com`, `*.wikipedia.org` and `*.wikivoyage.org`. No extension test is ever live. |

## 13.4 End-to-end acceptance scenarios

The primary journey is covered by nine scenarios. All automated ones run in Playwright against the Supabase CLI local stack (IMD-03), the API with `AI_PROVIDER=MOCK` and the Sampleton seed. Test users are created per run through the local service-role key (`e2e/fixtures/users.ts`). Every scenario runs an axe scan on each page it visits; a serious or critical violation fails the run. `journey.spec.ts` chains E2E-01 to E2E-06 as the single whole-journey test used by IMP-216 and IMP-414.

| ID | Scenario | Preconditions | Steps | Expected result | Spec file | Provider | Related |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E2E-01 | Create or sign in to an account | Local stack running; email confirmation off locally | Sign up with a new email; sign out; sign in; open `/dashboard` directly while signed out | Signed-in user lands on `/dashboard`; signed-out visit redirects to `/sign-in`; duplicate sign-up shows a non-revealing message | `auth.spec.ts` | None | FR-001, FR-002; TC-052, TC-055 |
| E2E-02 | Create a trip | Signed in; Sampleton seeded | `/trips/new`: destination Sampleton, 3 days, 2 travellers, budget, pace, two interests, two must-visit places; try an end date before the start date first | Field error shown and nothing saved for the invalid date; after correcting, trip appears on `/dashboard` with status draft or ready | `trip-create.spec.ts` | None | FR-007 to FR-010, FR-013; TC-071; ACC-01 |
| E2E-03 | Generate an itinerary | Trip from E2E-02; `MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO=ok` | Accept the privacy notice; press Generate; watch progress | Progress passes through the statuses; itinerary page opens with 3 days, times, labels and provider `MOCK`; no fallback notice | `generate.spec.ts` | MOCK; LIVE variant TC-370 (manual on staging) | FR-024, FR-025, FR-059; ACC-01, ACC-02 |
| E2E-04 | Validate the itinerary and its costs | Trip generated with `MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO=flawed` (one overlap, one missing must-visit place) and a budget set just above the estimate so the total exceeds 90 percent | Open the warnings panel; open `/trips/[tripId]/costs` | `OVERLAP` and `BUDGET_NEAR` (or `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`) shown with fixes; daily and category breakdown; every non-curated price labelled Estimate or Unavailable; totals equal the API values | `validate-costs.spec.ts` | MOCK | FR-050, FR-054, FR-071, FR-073, FR-076; ACC-06, ACC-07 |
| E2E-05 | Edit or remove an activity | Generated itinerary | Move one item with the keyboard move controls; change a duration; remove one item | Each edit shows the saving state, then recalculated times, costs and findings from the response; a removed must-visit item produces a warning | `itinerary-edit.spec.ts` | MOCK | FR-060, FR-061, FR-063, FR-064; TC-201; ACC-05, ACC-16 |
| E2E-06 | Save and reopen the trip | Edited itinerary from E2E-05 | Sign out; sign in; open the latest itinerary from the dashboard; open it in a second tab, edit in tab 1, then edit in tab 2 | Plan and warnings exactly as saved; tab 2 gets the reload message (409 `STALE_PLAN`) | `reopen.spec.ts` | MOCK | FR-013, FR-014, FR-069; TC-217; ACC-10, ACC-18 |
| E2E-07 | Handle an AI provider failure | Separate Playwright project `provider-failure` (IMD-33): API on port 8001 and web app on 3001, API started with `MOCK_PROVIDER_SCENARIO=timeout` (and a second run with `quota`) | Generate for a trip that has an earlier saved version; then edit and save | Fallback notice "Built by rules…" and outcome `fallback_rule_based` (timeout), or quota message with the rule-based option (quota); earlier version and trip data unchanged; editing still works | `provider-failure.spec.ts` | MOCK (scenarios) | FR-036, FR-037; TC-371, TC-308; ACC-03, ACC-17 |
| E2E-08 | Another user cannot access a private trip | Users A and B; A has a trip with an itinerary | As B, open A's `/trips/[tripId]/itinerary`, `/costs` and `/versions` URLs | Not-found page each time; no data from A's trip in the page or network responses | `ownership.spec.ts` | MOCK | FR-005; TC-375; ACC-08 |
| E2E-09 | Smoke-test the deployed application | Deployed staging or production; `BASE_URL` and API URL set | `make smoke URL=<api>`; `BASE_URL=<web> make e2e ARGS='--grep @smoke'`: health, readiness, landing page, sign-in page, protected route returns 401 without token; on staging also sign in with the smoke account and run one generation | All checks pass; readiness reports database ok and the active provider; staging generation ends `completed` (model or fallback) | `smoke.spec.ts`, `tests/smoke/test_deployed.py` | Environment's provider (GEMINI on staging: LIVE) | FR-123; TC-288, TC-289, TC-044, TC-377 |

Extensions add no scenario IDs. `apps/web/e2e/extensions.spec.ts`, tagged `@ext`, extends E2E-02 (describe a trip and confirm the proposal), E2E-05 (explain a day, optimise a day, swap days from a mocked rain forecast, apply a budget-fit suggestion, open the today view and the packing list) and E2E-08 (user B on A's `/today` and `/packing` URLs gets the not-found page). Each step is skipped with the switch reason when its extension is disabled (§13.1). Booking has no scenario (excluded, §1.3 and IMD-46).

Mock versus live: E2E-01 to E2E-08 and the `@ext` steps never call Gemini, OpenRouteService, Open-Meteo or MediaWiki. E2E-03 has a LIVE variant (TC-370) run by hand on staging under the spending cap, and E2E-09 is live by nature on a deployed environment; both are reported as live checks, not as CI results.

## 13.5 Regression policy

| Change | Must re-run before merge |
| --- | --- |
| Any change | `make check` (lint, types, imports, OpenAPI check, unit, contract, API, authz, web) |
| Prompt template, `PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION`, request builder, output schema io-1 | Contract suite; generation API tests; `make eval DATASET=trips/v1 PROVIDER=MOCK` regression subset; a GEMINI evaluation run by hand before the next gate, recorded in `eval/reports/` |
| `GEMINI_MODEL_ID` or adapter settings | Contract suite with recorded responses; new recordings captured with `make live-smoke` and reviewed; GEMINI evaluation run before the change reaches production |
| Validator rules, repair, finding codes or severities | All `unit/validation` cases; generation and edit API tests; E2E-04 and E2E-05; evaluation regression subset |
| Budget engine, labels, rounding | All `unit/budget` cases; costs API tests; E2E-04 |
| Migrations or ORM models | `make db-reset`; schema drift; full `make test-api` and `make test-authz` |
| Assistive prompt template (`trip_intake`, `day_explanation`, `packing_refine`) or ti-1, de-1, ps-1 (EXT) | `tests/unit/itinerary/test_explanation_check.py`, the contract suite, the endpoint's API tests (`test_trip_intake.py`, `test_day_explanation.py`, `test_packing.py`), the extension evaluation cases of the task card; `docs/model-change-log.md` entry |
| Open-Meteo or MediaWiki client, rain or context rules (EXT) | `unit/weather`, `unit/context` with recorded responses; `tests/api/test_weather_swap.py`, `test_context.py`; `@ext` E2E |
| A new endpoint | Its API tests; an ownership case in `tests/authz/` (the route inventory test fails otherwise); OpenAPI regenerated |
| Before each gate (§14) and before release | Full regression: `make check`, `make e2e`, `make eval DATASET=trips/v1 PROVIDER=MOCK`, deployment smoke on staging |

The evaluation regression subset is the cases of dataset v1 tagged `regression` in its manifest (Proposed: at least 5 of the 15 trips, including the must-visit, budget-tight and closed-day cases). The harness compares metrics with the last accepted report; a drop in schema validity, valid place IDs or feasibility on MOCK fails the run, while GEMINI comparisons are reviewed by M6 and M2 and recorded, not automated.

## 13.8 Coverage and thresholds (Proposed)

| Measure | Threshold | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Statement coverage, `app/validation` and `app/budget` | At least 85 percent | NFR-030 (Proposed) |
| Statement coverage, other backend modules | At least 70 percent | NFR-030 (Proposed) |
| Web unit coverage of `lib/format`, `lib/api` and the label components | At least 70 percent | Proposed here |
| High-priority MVP and MVP-S test cases implemented | All by the feature freeze (end of Sprint 6), or the shortfall listed and the cut order of blueprint §27.8 applied | Blueprint §27.7 |
| Ownership coverage | Every owned MVP and EXT route has a two-user case (TC-345, TC-431); enforced by the route-inventory test | TC-345 |
| Accessibility | No serious or critical axe violation on MVP pages and enabled EXT pages | NFR-025 |
| Edit recalculation time | p95 at most 1.5 s for a 10-day fixture on staging | NFR-003, TC-330 (Proposed) |
| Release | Every High-priority MVP test executed and passed or carrying a recorded exception; no open severity-1 defect | Blueprint §27.7 |

Defect severities (IMD-41, blueprint §27.11): 1 = journey blocked or data exposed; 2 = a feature of the journey fails without a workaround; 3 = a feature fails with a workaround; 4 = cosmetic. Severity 1 and 2 defects block a gate.

Thresholds are targets for the team, not results. A coverage figure is reported only from a CI coverage report of the commit in question.

# 14. Integration and release gates

**Rule.** No sprint is complete merely because code has been generated. A sprint is complete only when the application builds from a clean clone, the tests named by the sprint's tasks and gate have run and passed (in CI or in a recorded local run), and the integrated behaviour has been demonstrated on the stated environment. Each gate is executed by its VERIFY task (IMP-N99; the journey check IMP-414 feeds SG-4) and recorded in `docs/progress/gates.md` with the date, the commit SHA, each criterion as met or not met, and a link to its evidence. A criterion without linked evidence counts as not met. None of the gates has been reached yet.

## 14.1 Sprint gates

Severities follow IMD-41: severity 1 blocks a journey or exposes data; severity 2 breaks a requirement with no workaround; severity 3 has a workaround; severity 4 is cosmetic. Severity 1 and 2 defects in the gate's scope block every gate.

**Contract stability rule.** Once a gate lists a contract as stable, changing it requires a Proposed entry in the decision register, the updated contract files (`contracts/`, migrations, §6 entry) and a passing contract test in the same pull request; the integration lead (Kirtan) approves.

**Shared cards.** 55 of the 108 cards touch more than one layer and are split into named parts with their own points. The member with the most points on a card leads it; where two members hold the same points the card's previous role owner leads (the destination 1 curation card is led by Jeel, as the plan states). The lead opens the GitHub issue, tracks the card's acceptance criteria and attaches the completion evidence. Everyone on a shared card follows four rules:

1. **Contract first.** All 36 MVP endpoints get their final shapes in Sprint 2 (IMP-214) and return 501 until built, so screen parts can start against the generated client on day 1 of a sprint. Each extension card declares its own endpoints on day 1 of its sprint in the same way (IMD-37).
2. **API part merges first.** The backend, database or AI part merges once its tests pass; the screen part merges after it (the wave rule of §14.2: start against stubs, merge after the prerequisites).
3. **One branch and pull request per part.** For example Het opens `feat/IMP-409-move-api` and Manasvi opens `feat/IMP-409-move-controls`; the lead's pull request closes the card.
4. **Review across the seam.** The API owner reviews the screen's pull request and the screen owner reviews the API's; each side checks the contract it depends on.

## 14.4 How contribution is tracked

A part counts as done, with its points credited to its owner, when its pull request merges to `main` with every required check green and its share of the card's acceptance criteria is shown by tests.

| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Week 1 set-up | All ten members are collaborators on the private repository; Kirtan sets branch protection on `main`, the merge setting (Rebase and merge only), CODEOWNERS, the `commit-msg` hook and the CI `attribution` job (IMP-102) |
| Board | The GitHub Projects board has one issue per task part, assigned to its owner and labelled with sprint and points |
| Branches | `feat\|fix\|chore/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>`, one branch per part |
| Commits | Authored and committed as the part's owner with the name and email of the team table, also when the operator runs Claude Code for the part (IMD-61); one author per commit, no `Co-authored-by:` line and no mention of AI tools; Conventional Commits starting with the task ID, for example `feat(itinerary): IMP-409 keyboard move controls` |
| Pull requests | Opened from the operator's account with the IMP-102 template (linked task and requirement IDs, what changed, tests run with result lines, screenshots, contract and migration questions), assigned to the part owner, reviewer named by the run prompt; the title names the part, for example `IMP-409 · move-controls part` |
| Reviews | Every pull request needs one approval from the named reviewer's own account (never the operator's account that opened it). CODEOWNERS also requires Kirtan plus one other owner for `contracts/`, migrations and `app/schemas/`, and Nidhi for `app/ai/` |
| Attribution | Merged with Rebase and merge only: rebasing keeps each commit's author, so every merged part stays credited to its owner on `main`; GitHub counts a commit for a member when its author email is linked to that member's account (IMD-63) |
| Integration | Kirtan, as integration lead, merges in dependency order, keeps `main` green, and resolves migration heads and contract conflicts; a red `main` stops merges until fixed |
| Progress | Each part's pull request adds `docs/progress/parts/IMP-NNN-<part-slug>.md` with its status, owner and evidence; the gate card compiles `docs/progress/sprint-N.md` from these records; the lead marks the card done when all parts are merged and the card's acceptance criteria are verified; the planner's ledger is rebuilt from them on RESYNC (Appendix D) |

## 14.5 Judgment calls in the allocation and role names

Equal load and a perfect role match could not both hold, so the plan made the decisions below (version 2 adds the extension rules); any can be changed at sprint planning, and the cut-list checkpoint (IMP-499) rebalances points if extensions or cut-list features are switched off.

| Decision | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Extensions are additive (version 2) | The nine selected extensions add 9 cards and 57 points (IMP-515, IMP-612, IMP-613, IMP-708 to IMP-713). The 370 points of version 1 keep their owners and parts. Each member gains 5 or 6 points, all in Sprints 5 to 7, which had the lowest loads; Sprint 8 stays free for the release. |
| Screens built by their feature's owner (13 points) | The frontend work exceeds what Manasvi and Krrish can carry, since Krrish also tests. Jeel builds the explore page, place detail drawer, saved-places panel, versions page and the context card (7); Malhar the PlacePicker and meal-slot display (3); Manal the trip actions menu (2); Het the profile page (1). Manasvi reviews all of them. |
| Ranking and the fallback planner go to the database pair | AI/ML would otherwise carry more than 80 points, so IMP-304 ranking and IMP-402 fallback planner go to Jeel and Malhar, the places-data owners; the ranking explanation (IMP-515) follows the ranking to Jeel. |
| Uneven weeks | Kirtan has 10 points in Sprint 1 against a team average of 4.7 and should start IMP-101 and IMP-102 before Sprint 1 if he can. Other peaks: Nidhi and Manya 11 each in Sprint 3, Manasvi 10 and Het 9 in Sprint 4, Het and Jeel 10 in Sprint 6, Krrish 10 in Sprint 7. 42 or 43 points is about 128 focused hours, roughly 16 hours a week, above the 12 assumed by AS-01. |
| Extensions are cut first | If the week 4 checkpoint (IMP-499) or a gate finds the team behind, extensions are switched off before any MVP cut-list feature, in the order packing, context cards, budget fit, Today view, rain swap, optimise order, day explanations, natural-language intake, ranking explanation. Their points then return to the MVP cards and testing of the same sprint. |
| The cut list moves points | If the week 4 checkpoint switches off cut-list features, the cards behind them lose points, most of them Het's, Jeel's, Manal's and Krrish's. Rebalance at that checkpoint by moving Sprint 7 testing and documentation parts to them. |
